# OpenAdapt

**Give your agent a program, not a mouse.**

The open-source, verified execution layer for computer-use agents.

[![CI](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/actions/workflows/main.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/actions/workflows/main.yml) [![Packages CI](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/actions/workflows/packages.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/actions/workflows/packages.yml) [![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/openadapt.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/openadapt/) [![Python 3.11–3.12](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.11%E2%80%933.12-blue)](https://www.python.org/downloads/) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-3e6b4f.svg)](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/LICENSE) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-community-5865F2?logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/yF527cQbDG)

[What it can do](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/CAPABILITIES.md) · [Documentation](https://docs.openadapt.ai) · [Quickstart](https://docs.openadapt.ai/tutorials/quickstart/) · [Live demo](https://app.openadapt.ai/demo) · [Website](https://openadapt.ai) · [Get updates](https://openadapt.ai/#updates) · [Discord](https://discord.gg/yF527cQbDG)

</div>

Wrap any AI agent with before-click checks, fresh-reload read-back, and signed Ed25519 receipts. **0% silent errors** (vs. 15% for unwrapped frontier models), **+12.5 pp** higher completion on HealthAdminBench, and **1,000x cheaper and 5x faster** on repeating workflows once compiled.

A computer-use agent looks at the screen and chooses every click again, on
every run. OpenAdapt lets a person record a task (once for a simple path, or a
few times with `openadapt compile --induce` to cover variations), or lets an AI
agent perform it once while OpenAdapt records it, ideally on test data, in a
web, Windows, macOS, Linux or remote-desktop app. It compiles the demonstration
into a program,
and your agent calls the program as one tool. The program runs with no model
calls and sends no screenshots anywhere. It confirms the right record before
each save, checks the save after it, and returns a plain outcome that says
how the save was checked. When anything doesn't match, it stops and tells your agent
instead of guessing.

## Clean-room benchmark summary

### Real-upgrade UI drift across 4 web apps (`N = 60`, Gitea / Vikunja / Memos / Mealie)

Evaluated across real upstream app upgrades with 100-run cost amortization (paired unwrapped `gpt-5.4` subset `N = 20`):

| System | Survival | Silent errors | Amortized cost / run | Warm p50 latency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **OpenAdapt (`CommitJIT`)** | **70.0%** (42/60) | **0.0%** (0/60) | **$0.000015** (1,188x cheaper than `gpt-5.4`) | **1.88 s** (5.1x faster) |
| Unwrapped `gpt-5.4` (paired `N = 20`) | 80.0% (16/20) | 15.0% (3/20) | $0.017824 | 9.53 s |
| Stagehand-style unverified self-heal | 71.7% (43/60) | 3.3% (2/60) | $0.000205 | 4.47 s |
| Static Playwright | 6.7% (4/60) | — | — | — |
| Prompt-AWM (ICML 2025) | 1.7% (1/60) | — | — | — |

### Zero-leak Stanford `HealthAdminBench` (`N = 24` paired, `gpt-5.4` + `claude-sonnet-5-5`, 132 real reloads)

| Metric | Unwrapped baseline | With OpenAdapt verification | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| Silent errors | 70.8% | **45.8%** | **-25.0 pp** (`p = 0.03125`, zero regressions) |
| Full task completion | 29.2% | **41.7%** | **+12.5 pp** |

External benchmark evidence comes from the 4-app real Docker upgrade suite above, Stanford `HealthAdminBench`, and external agent-safety evaluations (`ST-WebAgentBench`, `OS-Harm`). Self-authored local fixtures are used only as developer smoke tests and unit tests, never as headline proof.

## Measured on OpenEMR and openIMIS

One new-patient referral in a test copy of OpenEMR, the open-source EHR whose
7.0 release is ONC-certified, timed from a fresh
browser through sign-in, the entry and the saved record read back (median):

| Who does the entry | Time per referral | Saved correctly | Model cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| Agent alone (Claude Sonnet 5.5 computer use) | `██████████████████` 36.5 s | 62 of 63 | about $0.08 |
| OpenAdapt program, screen steps | `███████████` 22.5 s | 18 of 18 | $0 |
| OpenAdapt program, API step | `██` 3.3 s | 18 of 18 | $0 |

The API step replaces the program's 41 screen steps with the one form
submission the app itself sends, then reads the record back. In both program
rows a possible-duplicate referral stopped without saving, as it should. Both
program rows ran on 19 Oct on one copy of the app, interleaved, with the
approval gate off; the benchmark harness admitted the API step. The agent row
is the 14 to 15 Oct timing study, on its own copy of the app.
[SCOREBOARD.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/benchmark/scoreboard/SCOREBOARD.md#openemr-agent-screen-program-and-api-step)
has every run.

On a test copy of openIMIS, the open-source insurance and claims system that
runs Nepal's national health insurance scheme, the compiled program entered
149 synthetic claims with no model calls: 148 read back correct and none were
saved wrong. Each saved claim was checked through a read-only database role on
the test copy; the 149th stopped before saving
([SCOREBOARD.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/benchmark/scoreboard/SCOREBOARD.md#openimis)).

## One harness, three modes

| Mode | What happens | Model calls |
|---|---|---|
| **Explore** | A person records the task (once, or several times with `openadapt compile --induce` for variations), or an AI agent runs it once while OpenAdapt records every action, ideally on test data. The save is checked before anything compiles. | Your agent's, on your own key |
| **Run** | The compiled program repeats the task with new inputs. It checks the record before each save and reads the result back after. | None |
| **Repair** | When the app changes, the run stops before saving. An agent shows the fix, the program tries it up to the save without saving, and a person approves it. | Only when something changed, on your own key |

## The 3-level verification ladder

Most enterprise deployments do not give an automation tool direct SQL access,
and OpenAdapt does not require it. OpenAdapt picks the strongest layer the app
supports:

- **Promote to API or MCP when an endpoint exists:** Record the task in the
  GUI, compile it into direct form/RPC calls and MCP tools (`openadapt-agent serve`)
  whenever the app exposes an endpoint, and avoid replaying pixels where a
  compiled API step is ~7x faster (3.3 s vs. 22.5 s on OpenEMR above).
- **Level 1 (Before-click local guard: 100% of apps, 0 DB needed):** Checks
  the active record and entity identity across tabs, enforces policy and
  consent gates before consequential writes, and checks screenshots locally for
  UI drift or prompt injection. If anything looks wrong, it stops and asks a
  person instead of guessing.
- **Level 2 (Post-action UI and confirmation read-back: ~90% of portals, 0 DB needed):**
  Reads back submitted fields, server confirmation IDs, or generated PDFs in a
  separate session to confirm what the portal actually recorded.
- **Level 3 (Direct API or DB read-back: optional upgrade):** When you own the
  system or have read-only FHIR, REST, or SQL access, reads the system of
  record directly and mints a signed `VERIFIED` receipt.

## 30-second local smoke test

```bash
uvx --python 3.12 openadapt@latest quickstart
```

No account or API key. [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/)
fetches Python 3.12 if you need it, and `@latest` runs the newest release. With
Python 3.11 or 3.12 already installed, `python -m pip install --upgrade openadapt`
then `openadapt quickstart` does the same. Add `--watch` to see the browser
window, or run `uvx --python 3.12 openadapt@latest quickstart --break-it` to
also walk through how a halted run and its local receipt appear in the terminal.

This quickstart is a local developer walkthrough against a bundled demo server
to verify your installation and inspect the CLI output. It is a smoke test, not
a benchmark or evidence of real-world failure rates; see the clean-room external
benchmarks above for empirical results. The
[quickstart tutorial](https://docs.openadapt.ai/tutorials/quickstart/) walks
through every step.

## Build with it

### Compile your agent's run

Your agent (Claude or OpenAI computer use, or your own loop, on your own model
key) does the task once while OpenAdapt records it, ideally on test data. A person reviews and admits
the draft program, or a registered agent admits it under a policy a person
signed. After that, the program runs instead of the agent.

```python
from openadapt_flow.jit import compile_agent

jit = compile_agent(my_agent, task=task, app=app, verifier=verifier,
                    policy="clinical-write", cache_dir="jit-cache", model_key=key)
jit.run(note="Follow up in two weeks")    # the agent does it; a DRAFT is saved
# a person reviews, runs the canary, and admits the draft
jit.run(note="Recheck knee in ten days")  # the program runs: 0 model calls, save read back
```

[Compile a computer-use agent's run](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/JIT.md) has the full
example. The same path takes an agent's run through the web, Windows, macOS,
Linux, RDP and Citrix backends.

### Call programs from your agent

```bash
claude mcp add openadapt -- uvx --python 3.12 openadapt-agent serve
```

Each compiled workflow becomes one tool call. The agent decides what to enter;
OpenAdapt makes the entry, checks it, and returns an outcome instead of the
agent driving the screen. With no bundles, the server offers a synthetic
sandbox workflow that returns every outcome. To serve your own workflows, run
`openadapt services agent serve --mode production --bundles ./bundles`; without
`--mode production` the agent can list them but not run them.
`openadapt-agent emit-skill <bundle>` writes an Agent Skill for one workflow,
and `openadapt verify effect` judges a write made by any agent or script
against the system of record. `openadapt hooks install --agent claude-code`
(or `codex`) checks a coding agent's writes to the databases, APIs and MCP
servers you declare: each is pre-checked, read back and given a signed
receipt. The hooks are advisory; see
[HOOKS.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/HOOKS.md).
[Connect an agent](https://docs.openadapt.ai/how-to/connect-an-agent/)
covers other clients.

### Hand results from agent to agent

When one agent hands a result to another, the run's signed receipt goes with
it, and the receiving agent verifies it against keys it pins:

```bash
openadapt handoff send result.json --run RUN_DIR --out result.handoff.json
openadapt handoff verify result.handoff.json --keys trusted-keys.json
```

The verdict says who signed, which checks passed and which were not checked,
and any change confirmed in the other party's own system. A valid signature
proves who signed, not that the claim is true. Handoffs travel over MCP
(`serve --handoffs`), HTTP and webhooks (`--post URL`), files and email
(`--detached`), and the A2A (Agent2Agent) protocol (`openadapt agent serve
--a2a`, with an Agent Card, after `pip install 'openadapt[a2a]'`).
[HANDOFFS.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/HANDOFFS.md)
has the details.

### Record a task by hand

Recording works the same way on every surface; only the target differs:
`--url` for a web app, `--window` (and `--window-title`) for a Windows or macOS
app window or a local RDP or Citrix client window. Linux and network RDP record
the whole local desktop, so they take no target.

```bash
python -m pip install --upgrade openadapt
openadapt record --backend <web|windows|macos|linux|rdp|citrix> <target> --out rec

# A web app
openadapt record --backend web --url https://staging.your-app.example --out rec
openadapt compile rec --out bundle --name my-first-workflow
openadapt run --replay bundle --url https://staging.your-app.example --run-dir run

# A desktop app (macOS here; Windows and Citrix take --window too).
# Desktop recording and macOS replay are separate extras.
python -m pip install --upgrade 'openadapt[capture,macos]'
openadapt record --backend macos --window "Your App" --out rec
openadapt compile rec --out bundle --name my-first-workflow
openadapt run --replay bundle --macos-app "Your App" --run-dir run
```

`run --replay` drives the app and performs every recorded action,
including saves you can't undo. It doesn't ask first and doesn't check the
saved record. Point it at a test or staging copy, never at production data.

The commands for every surface, including Linux, RDP and Citrix, are in
[SURFACES.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/SURFACES.md#first-workflow-per-surface).

The existing engine command remains available for scripts:

```bash
openadapt flow replay bundle --url https://staging.your-app.example --run-dir run
```

`flow replay` performs every recorded action, including real saves. Use a test
or staging copy; it does not ask for approval or check the saved record.

A program that writes to a real system also needs record checks, a deployment
file, certification, qualification, and an admission; then `openadapt run`
runs it. By default each save waits for a person to approve it in OpenAdapt
Desktop or on a paired phone. [Your first workflow](https://docs.openadapt.ai/tutorials/first-workflow/)
walks through it. Several recordings of the same task can become one program
with branches and loops (`openadapt compile --induce`).

To record a desktop app, install the recorder and your operating system's
adapter, for example `python -m pip install "openadapt[capture,windows]"`, or
use [OpenAdapt Desktop](https://openadapt.ai/download).

`openadapt --help` lists the task commands. `openadapt wrap --help` shows the
options for running an agent task once and reusing its checked compiled tool.
The [CLI reference](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/docs/cli.md) lists task paths and their original aliases.

### Judge or train any agent

`openadapt verify effect` judges a write made by any agent or script against
the system of record. `openadapt-flow services reward` turns the same check into a
reward for training or evaluating computer-use agents
([REWARD_WORKER.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/REWARD_WORKER.md)).

## An agent alone, and an OpenAdapt program

The same referral task on a local OpenEMR 8.0.0.3 test copy with synthetic
patients, 62 timed runs each (14 and 15 October 2026), judged by the same
database read-back:

| | Claude computer-use agent | OpenAdapt program |
|---|---|---|
| Model calls | On every step of every run | 0 |
| Screenshots sent to a model | Throughout every run | 0 |
| Model cost per referral | About $0.08 at list price | $0 |
| Path through the app | Chosen again each run | The same compiled steps |
| Median time | 36.5 s | 29.7 s |
| Referrals saved correctly | 62 of 63 | 62 of 63 |

The program drove every page, as the agent does. The API step compiled from
the recording's network traffic removes those page steps: 3.3 s per referral,
in the table at the top. [Every result](https://openadapt.ai/compare/computer-use-agents)
is published. OpenAdapt isn't affiliated with the OpenEMR project.

## Every backend

**Web apps are the production-mature surface** (DOM structure, fresh-reload
read-back, compiled API promotion, self-repair, and rollback). Native desktop
(Windows, macOS, Linux), RDP, and Citrix backends share the same record,
compile, and run pipeline with narrower documented boundaries
([BACKEND_PARITY.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/BACKEND_PARITY.md)). Self-repair is
qualified on browser runs ([benchmark/auto_repair](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/benchmark/auto_repair/README.md))
and end to end on native macOS AX ([#1715](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1715)). Outside a browser it
runs with `repair.session` ([#1717](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1717)), and native and pixel backends admit
its new clicks by element identity ([#1709](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1709)). Teaching the fix for a
halted run and rollback are tested on browser runs. Where
the app exposes its structure, OpenAdapt uses it; on remote desktops it works
from pixels.

| Surface | Maturity & boundaries | What OpenAdapt reads | Validated on |
|---|---|---|---|
| Web apps | Production-mature (DOM, reload read-back, API promotion, repair, rollback) | The screen, plus the page's DOM | Gitea, Vikunja, Memos, Mealie, OpenEMR, Odoo, and openIMIS; CI runs in-tree apps on every build |
| Windows apps | Documented boundary (UI Automation; per-app qualification required) | The screen, plus UI Automation | 3 of 3 saves in a WinForms test app |
| macOS apps | Documented boundary (Accessibility; per-app qualification required) | The screen, plus Accessibility | 3 of 3 saves in TextEdit |
| Linux apps (X11) | Documented boundary (AT-SPI; X11 only) | The screen, plus AT-SPI | Recording and an AT-SPI read in CI; backend actions are unit-tested |
| Remote desktop (RDP) | Documented boundary (pixel-only; higher false-stop rate on visual drift) | The screen | 105 runs through the stock Remote Desktop client on a real AVC444 session: 55 saves confirmed in the database, 0 wrong-record saves, 40 false stops |
| Citrix | Documented boundary (pixel-only; per-app qualification required) | The screen | A Citrix stand-in app with no DOM: 3 healthy runs, 3 stops on drift |

Each application on each surface needs its own qualification.
[Surfaces](https://docs.openadapt.ai/explanation/surfaces/) and [Limits](https://docs.openadapt.ai/explanation/limits/)
have the details.

## How it works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    S["Demonstrate (human or AI agent)"] --> C["Compile"] --> Q["Certify and qualify"] --> A["Admit"] --> R["Run with checks"]
    R -.->|"stopped: approve a fix"| C
```

For each step the compiler uses the most reliable layer the app offers: page
structure first (DOM, Windows UI Automation, macOS Accessibility, Linux
AT-SPI), a direct API call where one is bound, and pixels (template, text and
layout matching) only where nothing else exists, such as a remote desktop.
Qualification runs the program against normal and fault cases before an
admission lets that exact version run. At each save the program checks that
the right record is on screen, makes the entry, and reads the record back.

## How it compares

| | Computer-use agent | Agent with a replay cache | Traditional RPA | OpenAdapt |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| How you define the task | A goal in plain language | One agent run | A script or flow built in a designer | A person's recording or an agent's run |
| What runs each time | A model chooses each step from the screen | The recorded steps; the agent takes over on a miss | The fixed script | A compiled program you can read |
| Model calls per run | At least one per step | None on a hit; the agent's calls on a miss | None | None with default settings |
| When the screen changes | The model tries to adapt | The agent improvises live | A selector stops matching, or matches the wrong control | The run stops before saving; a fix is proposed and a person approves it |
| Right record? | The model judges from the screen | Usually only that the screen looks as recorded | Whatever the developer scripted | Checked before every save |
| Did the save land? | The model judges from the screen | The screen | Whatever the developer scripted | Reported verified only when a read outside the acting session confirms it; weaker checks are named as such |
| Strongest for | New or changing tasks | Repeated tasks where a wrong save is cheap | Stable processes with a team to maintain the scripts | The same entry many times, where a wrong save is costly |

## What it can do

- **Learns from any successful run**, a person's demonstration or a computer-use agent's verified run, and compiles it into a program that runs with no calls to a hosted AI model.
- **Uses the most reliable layer the app allows**: page structure (DOM, UI Automation, Accessibility), direct API calls where one is bound, and pixels only for remote desktops.
- **Builds branching programs** from several demonstrations, repeated halts and background runs, and routes each item to the right verified variant.
- **Works across surfaces**: web, Windows, macOS, Linux and RDP backends, chained in one workflow.
- **Confirms the right record before every write and checks the saved record after it**. A run is reported verified only when a read outside the acting session confirms the save: the system of record where one can be read, or a separate session. Weaker checks are reported at their own level.
- **Stops instead of guessing**, never retries an uncertain save, and says what changed before a stop.
- **Binds each approval to exactly what will be saved**, with one-tap answers on a paired phone.
- **Repairs itself when the app changes**, probing a fix up to the save and asking a person to approve it (qualified on browser runs and end to end on native macOS).
- **Works as a safety layer under any agent**: MCP tools, a guarded save, Agent Skills and a CLI.
- **Hands results from agent to agent with their receipts**, over MCP, HTTP, files and the A2A protocol, and verifies a handoff on arrival.
- **Runs locally**: no calls to a hosted AI model on healthy runs, personal and health data redacted, signed receipts.

[CAPABILITIES.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/CAPABILITIES.md) has the evidence and code for each.

## What your agent gets back

| You see | `transaction_outcome` | An agent gets | What happens next |
|---|---|---|---|
| Done and checked | `VERIFIED` | `done` | Nothing. Only this result gets a shareable receipt. |
| Stopped before saving | `HALTED_BEFORE_EFFECT` | `needs_review` | Fix the cause, or show the program the fix, and run again. |
| Check the record | `RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED` | `not_sure_if_saved` | A save may have gone through. A person checks the record before anything is retried. |
| Finished, not checked | `COMPLETED_UNVERIFIED` | `not_sure_if_saved` | Fine for testing; not a production success. |
| Saved, waiting for its check | `SAVED_AWAITING_CHECK` | `not_sure_if_saved` | The save's check is a later report (a claim acknowledgment, an export). Don't rerun it. `openadapt-flow verify deferred settle` counts it as done only when the report confirms it. |
| Didn't run | `REJECTED_POLICY`, `CANCELED`, `FAILED_PLATFORM` | `did_not_run` | Fix the gate or the environment and run again. |

The console's last line can read `HALTED` for both the second and third rows.
`transaction_outcome` in `report.json` tells them apart, so base every rerun on
it. [Run outcomes](https://docs.openadapt.ai/reference/outcomes/) lists every value.

## When to use something else

- **You already have a clean, documented API client for the task.** Call the
  API directly. (If the app only exposes an internal form or RPC endpoint,
  OpenAdapt can record it in the GUI and compile it into a direct API/MCP
  step instead of replaying pixels.)
- **Every task is one-off.** Use a computer-use agent. OpenAdapt pays off when
  the same entry repeats or needs repeatable verification.
- **You need a `VERIFIED` receipt with zero read-back path at all.** Level 1
  before-click guards work on 100% of apps with no database access, and Level 2
  UI confirmation read-back covers ~90% of portals with no database access.
  Level 3 direct API/FHIR/SQL read-back is an optional upgrade when you own the
  system. If a target exposes neither a UI read-back nor an API/DB read-back, a
  run finishes as checked-before-click (`COMPLETED_UNVERIFIED`) rather than
  `VERIFIED`.


## Packages

`pip install openadapt` installs the `openadapt` command, the engine, and the
MCP server. The product packages live in this repository:

| Package (PyPI) | What it is | Source |
|---|---|---|
| [`openadapt`](https://pypi.org/project/openadapt/) | The `openadapt` command | [`openadapt/`](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/tree/main/openadapt) |
| [`openadapt-flow`](https://pypi.org/project/openadapt-flow/) | The engine: record, compile, check, qualify, run, repair | [`packages/flow/`](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/tree/main/packages/flow) |
| [`openadapt-agent`](https://pypi.org/project/openadapt-agent/) | The MCP server and Agent Skills | [`packages/agent/`](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/tree/main/packages/agent) |
| [`openadapt-types`](https://pypi.org/project/openadapt-types/) | Shared request, result, and receipt models | [`packages/types/`](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/tree/main/packages/types) |
| [`openadapt-capture`](https://pypi.org/project/openadapt-capture/) | The desktop recorder: `openadapt[capture]` | [`packages/capture/`](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/tree/main/packages/capture) |
| [`openadapt-privacy`](https://pypi.org/project/openadapt-privacy/) | Finds and redacts personal and health data: `openadapt[privacy]` | [`packages/privacy/`](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/tree/main/packages/privacy) |
| [`openadapt-desktop`](https://pypi.org/project/openadapt-desktop/) | OpenAdapt Desktop ([download](https://openadapt.ai/download)) | [`packages/desktop/`](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/tree/main/packages/desktop) |
| [`openadapt-tray`](https://pypi.org/project/openadapt-tray/) | Menu-bar and system-tray controls and status for OpenAdapt Desktop | [`packages/tray/`](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/tree/main/packages/tray) |

Each package installs only what it imports. For example, `pip install openadapt-privacy` doesn't install the engine or the desktop app. CI checks each package's install size and dependency list ([install weight](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/docs/monorepo/INSTALL_WEIGHT.md)).

Research on GUI agents lives in separate repositories:
[openadapt-evals](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/openadapt-evals) (benchmarks)
and [openadapt-ml](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/openadapt-ml) (model
training). The [packages map](https://docs.openadapt.ai/reference/packages/) has the full list.

## Security and procurement

Screens, typed values, and recordings stay on the computer or runner that runs
OpenAdapt. The shareable receipt and the Cloud dashboard hold counts, digests,
and closed values. A sanitized copy leaves only after a person approves it, and
screenshots go to a model host only if you turn on model grounding.
[Security & procurement](https://docs.openadapt.ai/security/) covers data handling, deployment
boundaries, evidence, subprocessors, and release integrity. Plans are on the
[pricing page](https://openadapt.ai/pricing).

<details>
<summary>Release status</summary>

The block below is generated from the signed public lifecycle record.

<!-- BEGIN PRODUCTION LIFECYCLE -->
The signed ledger has seven active target admissions. Their evidence class
is `remote-safe-synthetic`, not MockMed `production_acceptance`. They remain
valid until revoked; there's no expiry date. `pip install openadapt` is the
admitted runtime (launcher 1.16.0, Flow 1.35.1). Desktop's admitted artifact
is the 0.16.0 wheel. Native Mac DMGs stay ad-hoc signed 0.15.0; don't treat
those as admitted. A Production run still needs a workflow admission for the
exact compiled bundle, application, and environment.
[Check the live signed Production record](https://docs.openadapt.ai/production-lifecycle.json).
<!-- END PRODUCTION LIFECYCLE -->

</details>

## Earlier versions

The pre-1.0 version (v0.46.0) is frozen under
[`legacy/`](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/tree/main/legacy).
[docs/LEGACY_FREEZE.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/docs/LEGACY_FREEZE.md)
explains how to install it and how to migrate.

# What OpenAdapt can do

OpenAdapt turns a task that a person or an AI agent does once in an
application into a program that repeats it with new inputs. The program makes
the same entry every time with no calls to a hosted AI model, checks that the
entry landed in the right record by reading it back, and stops instead of
guessing. It is for web, desktop and remote-desktop applications with no
usable API. EMRs and payer portals are examples of highly regulated settings
where those checks matter most.

This page indexes what OpenAdapt implements, with the status, the evidence and
the code for each capability:

- [Ten capabilities](#openadapt-in-ten-capabilities) and [often missed](#often-missed)
- [The core: a checked entry](#the-core-a-checked-entry-every-time),
  [approvals](#approvals), [branching work](#branching-work-not-one-linear-path)
- [Surfaces](#surfaces), [the fastest layer](#the-fastest-layer-the-app-allows),
  [when the app changes](#when-the-app-changes)
- [Computer-use agents](#computer-use-agents),
  [recording, privacy and proof](#recording-privacy-and-proof)
- [Every command](#every-command-by-capability) and
  [measured results](#measured-results)

## OpenAdapt in ten capabilities

Each capability is implemented in the
[OpenAdapt monorepo](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt). "Released"
means it ships in the current PyPI packages; "on main" means merged into the
monorepo and installable from source.

1. **Learns from any successful run, a person's or an agent's.** A person
   records a task, or a computer-use agent does it once and OpenAdapt compiles
   the verified run into a program (`openadapt_flow.jit`, released;
   prompt-to-program `compile-agent`, on main; the agent acts through code by
   default, not screenshots, and every save the gate detects in its run is read
   back, [#1305](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1305)). Agents can drive the recording
   through the web, native Windows, RDP and Citrix backends. An agent connected over MCP can
   teach itself a new workflow and then call it as a tool
   (`openadapt-agent serve --teach`,
   [#1335](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1335)).
2. **Compiles to the fastest layer the app allows.** Page structure first (DOM,
   Windows UI Automation, macOS Accessibility), direct API calls where the app's
   own traffic allows them (`ApiActuator`, released; compiled from captured
   traffic in [#1261](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1261)),
   and pixels only
   where nothing else exists, such as a remote desktop. It is not a pixel-macro
   recorder.
3. **Builds branching programs, not one linear path.** One program from several
   demonstrations (`induce`, `disambiguate`), a branch learned from several
   halts fixed the same way (`teach-branch`), candidate branches mined from many
   real runs in the background (shadow mode,
   [#1212](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1212)), and a router
   that sends each item to the right verified variant. Shadow mining and the
   router are on main; the rest is released.
4. **Works across surfaces in one workflow.** Backends for web, native Windows
   and macOS, Linux, RDP and Citrix. Programs chain across surfaces passing confirmed values
   (`compose`, `process`, released), and one program can switch surfaces, tabs
   and popups mid-run ([#1197](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1197)).
5. **Confirms the right record before every write and reads it back after.**
   A run is `VERIFIED` only when a read outside the acting session confirms the
   save: the system of record (API, database, FHIR with SMART Backend Services,
   a log or an export) or a separate session (a fresh sign-in on the web; on
   desktop, a fresh session or a relaunch of the app, as the deployment
   declares). A read on the acting screen gets its own level and never
   verifies a run. The run report names the level for each save with a
   declared read-back. Where the app's own screens are the only independent
   read, the check covers at most the target record, plus the same actor's
   changes in the app's activity log within a stated window where the app
   shows one and the program is set up to read it; other records, later
   server-side jobs and outbound messages are not covered. The wire check is
   evidence of what was sent, not a check level.
   `record --verify` proposes those checks from what the demonstration changed.
   Released.
6. **Stops instead of improvising, and never retries an uncertain save.** A run
   that can't prove a save ends `HALTED_BEFORE_EFFECT` or
   `RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED`, never "success". A ledger of what changed before
   a stop, with undo steps a person approves, is on main. The rest is
   released.
7. **Approvals are bound to exactly what will be saved.** Each save waits for a
   person by default and can be answered on a paired phone with one card per
   decision. The approval is bound to the exact screenshot and form state, and
   the form is read again before saving, so what was approved is what is saved.
   Person-signed grants let named agents answer. Released.
8. **Repairs itself, with a person approving.** Governed repair (propose,
   review, campaign, canary, rollback), agent-demonstrated fixes for a halted
   run, and fleet drift patches shared with no patient data (moved as files
   or through a local reference hub) are released.
   Self-repair, where an agent proposes a fix and Flow probes it up to the save
   without saving, is on main, and so are fixes of up to three new steps.
   Self-repair is qualified on browser runs ([benchmark/auto_repair](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/benchmark/auto_repair/README.md))
   and end to end on native macOS AX ([#1715](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1715)). Outside a browser it
   runs with `repair.session` ([#1717](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1717)), and native and pixel backends
   admit its new clicks by element identity ([#1709](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1709)). Teaching the fix
   for a halted run (`--hold-on-halt`) and rollback are tested on browser runs.
9. **Is a safety layer underneath any agent.** An agent's MCP calls, a task
   ledger that keeps a long job's rules, items, questions and checked saves on
   the server ([#1332](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1332)), a guarded save around any agent's write
   ([#1258](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1258)), a guard for
   an agent you already run that holds its browser's saves with no change to
   the agent ([#1357](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1357)), `verify-run`
   to judge any executor's write from the system of record, and Agent Skills and
   a CLI for coding agents. Released except where a PR is named.
10. **Runs locally and keeps data private.** Healthy runs make no calls to a
    hosted AI model and send nothing out. Personal and health data are redacted from text,
    screenshots and structure (scrub-by-default for anything that leaves the
    machine is on main); a strict no-outbound mode, an unattended on-prem
    service, and signed, timestamped receipts are released.

## Often missed

| What OpenAdapt does | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Learns branching programs from several demonstrations, from repeated halts, and from many background runs. | `induce`, `teach-branch`, [SHADOW_MINING.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/capture/docs/SHADOW_MINING.md), [LEARN_FROM_MANY_RUNS.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/LEARN_FROM_MANY_RUNS.md) |
| Chains programs across surfaces, and one program can switch surfaces, tabs and popups mid-run. | `compose`, `process`, [#1197](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1197) |
| Uses page structure first on web, Windows, macOS and Linux, with pixels as the fallback for remote desktops. Benchmarks labelled "vision-only" ran a deliberately pixel-only arm. | [RESOLUTION_LADDER.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/RESOLUTION_LADDER.md) |
| Replaces a single HTML form submission with the request the app itself sends, compiled from the network traffic captured while recording, then reads the record back. URL-encoded and file-less multipart saves, the clicked button's value, and saves the page's script sends to another endpoint are covered. JSON saves (GraphQL mutations included) are bound by JSON pointer and sent with the headers the app's own script sends in the session. Uploads, multi-step wizards and governed runs still use the screen steps. | `api`, [API_TIER.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/API_TIER.md) |
| Builds the record check itself. After a save, the app usually reads the record back to show it; `scaffold-verifier` finds that read in the captured traffic or a read-only database, builds the check from it and tries to break it before a person reviews it. No API or SQL needs to be written by hand. | [EFFECT_KIT.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/EFFECT_KIT.md#a-record-check-built-from-the-apps-own-reads-scaffold-verifier) |
| Checks a save on desktop, RDP and Citrix apps with no API at all, by looking the record up in the app's own screens in a separate session. | [EFFECT_KIT.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/EFFECT_KIT.md#separate-session-desktop-read-back-desktop_readback) |
| Reads a web save back a second time when the app has no API or database read: a separate, freshly signed-in session reads a search view the save didn't show, counts duplicates, reads the app's audit log for collateral changes, and settles portal saves that are "pending review" with a later read. It is graded a screen read-back, never the system-of-record check. On OpenEMR and Dolibarr, direct or behind a bad-VPN proxy, the only planted fault it confirmed was a collateral edit when no audit view was declared. | [EFFECT_KIT.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/EFFECT_KIT.md#when-a-ui-read-counts), [benchmark/ui_second_read](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/benchmark/ui_second_read/RESULTS.md) |
| Keeps pixel-path runs working across display scaling from 100% to 175% and font smoothing on or off, and stops rather than saves when the record changed. | [benchmark/pixel_scale](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/benchmark/pixel_scale/README.md) |
| Lists every change made before a stop and rolls it back with compensations a person approved once, then proves it by reading the whole database: equal to the read from before the run is `ROLLED_BACK`, anything else names the exact rows. | `undo`, `rollback`, [ROLLBACK.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/ROLLBACK.md), [AFTER_A_STOP.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/AFTER_A_STOP.md) |
| Clears a known interruption (a session warning, a banner, a tour) by itself, only when the dismissal is provably read-only: matched by its text and control, a closed set of non-committing labels, no write seen by the browser write fence or the system-of-record read-back, and the step's normal identity check afterwards. Anything else stops the run. Classes are per-app data. | [INTERRUPTION_RECOVERY.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/INTERRUPTION_RECOVERY.md) |
| Repairs itself when the app changes: governed repair, agent-demonstrated fixes, fleet patches, and self-repair probed up to the save. | [REPAIR_LIFECYCLE.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/REPAIR_LIFECYCLE.md) |
| Repairs a change that needs new steps, such as a new required dialog or a control moved into a menu: up to three new steps, each with its own record check, probed up to the save before one person approves. | [SELF_REPAIR.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/SELF_REPAIR.md), [#1325](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1325) |
| Compiles a computer-use agent's verified run, with no human demonstration needed. | [JIT.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/JIT.md) |
| The agent that does a task once acts through code by default, not a screenshot-and-click loop: it reads the page or accessibility tree, acts by role and name, keeps notes with a sandboxed read-only shell, and asks for a screenshot only when it needs one. Every save the save gate detects is read back from the system of record before the agent goes on. Scoreboard arm 7, MockMed items 21 to 40: 18 of 18 normal items correct at $0.0093 an item; the wrong-patient save landed and the read-back then stopped the run; the scoreboard counts 1 silent wrong save by its word rule, a safe stop on hand review ([HAND_REVIEW.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/benchmark/scoreboard/raw/mockmed/code_agent/2026-10-25-rb/HAND_REVIEW.md)). The program compiled from it: 18 of 18 at $0. | `CODE_AS_ACTION.md` in [#1305](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1305) |
| Binds each approval to the exact screenshot and form state, and re-reads the form before saving. | [APPROVAL_MODES.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/APPROVAL_MODES.md) |
| Has a written threat model for prompt injection against the agent that teaches or repairs a program, with tests. | [THREAT_MODEL.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/THREAT_MODEL.md) |
| Fills inputs from a referral PDF, fax image or email, and holds back anything unclear for a person. | `intake`, [INTAKE.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/INTAKE.md) |
| Ships as one monorepo with separately installable packages (flow, agent, types, capture, privacy, desktop and tray), each released from the monorepo. | [README](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/README.md) |
| Makes no calls to a hosted AI model on healthy runs. Model training (openadapt-ml) is separate research. | [README](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/README.md) |

## The full map

Every capability, with its status, its evidence and where it lives.

Status:

- **Released**: in the current releases: `openadapt` 1.19.0 and openadapt-flow
  2.5.0 on PyPI, and Desktop 0.25.0 for Desktop rows.
- **On main**: merged into the monorepo; installable from source.

Evidence:

- **Real app**: run against a real third-party application, such as a local
  OpenEMR or openIMIS.
- **Synthetic**: run against OpenAdapt's own test apps (MockMed and fixtures).

All patient and claim data in every test and benchmark is synthetic.

## The core: a checked entry, every time

A person, or a computer-use agent once, shows a task. OpenAdapt compiles it
into a program that makes the same entry every time with no model calls. It
confirms the right record before acting, reads the saved record back from the
system of record instead of trusting the screen, and stops instead of
improvising or retrying when something is off.

| Capability | Status | Evidence | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Compile one or more demonstrations into a deterministic program | Released | Real app (OpenEMR referral, 62 timed runs) | `openadapt-flow record`, `compile`; [packages/flow](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/README.md) |
| Try the three acts on a real app: `openadapt quickstart --app openemr` runs the certified OpenEMR referral program in Docker, five referrals at once checked in OpenEMR's record, then a possible duplicate stopped before saving; without Docker or a clone it says so and exits 2 | On main ([#1431](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1431)) | Real app (local OpenEMR 8.0.0.3, synthetic patients) | `openadapt quickstart --app openemr`; [docs/quickstart](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/docs/quickstart/README.md#on-a-real-app---app-openemr) |
| Run the quickstart without taking over the screen: `uvx --python 3.12 openadapt@latest quickstart` keeps the browser hidden and shows progress in the terminal (`--watch` shows the window, `--open` opens the Seal page), runs a run whose starting screen never settles once more in a new folder and otherwise says why in plain words, and reruns itself with Python 3.12 under `uvx` on an unsupported Python. Flow's page settle hands a page that draws no frames (a covered headed window) to the screenshot check instead of waiting out its timeout | On main ([#2365](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/2365)) | Unit tests; headless terminal captures at 80, 120 and 250 columns for Terminal.app, WezTerm and iTerm2 settings; a headed covered-window run is not reproduced here | `openadapt quickstart`; [openadapt/quickstart](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/openadapt/quickstart/__init__.py), [_page_quiescence.py](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/openadapt_flow/backends/_page_quiescence.py) |
| Classify common local edits without a person (select-all, Enter in a field or dropdown, an in-form tab, an informational dialog's dismiss), only when the recording's network capture shows no write and a runtime check confirms only the expected change | Released ([#1366](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1366)) | Synthetic; OpenEMR referral recording re-admitted offline (violations 12 to 1 under `permissive`) | [LOCAL_EDIT_CLASSIFICATION.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/design/LOCAL_EDIT_CLASSIFICATION.md), `compiler/local_edit.py` |
| Keep the empty search result a person confirmed through (a duplicate check's "No matches were found.") as an exact check after the click that opens the dialog and again right before Confirm, so a run whose dialog lists a match stops before the save; only fixed-vocabulary search-result statements shown once, never text with a name or search term, and a confirmation dialog without one is noted in `compile_notes.json` | On main | Real app frames (an OpenEMR referral recording, compiled offline) | `compiler/empty_result_guard.py` |
| Mine that check in any language: induction keeps the one line a named dialog adds (not its title or buttons, not a question, no typed value or number) when two or more demonstrations whose typed values all differ show the same line, refuses when the demonstrations disagree on a mined check instead of copying the first one's, and qualification then needs a business-rule run that halts at it | On main | Synthetic (a search dialog recorded in Chromium by the real recorder, German statement, real OCR) | `compiler/empty_result_guard.py`, `compiler/induction.py` |
| Qualify against a rule the app itself enforces: verify.yaml `business_rules` seed the conflicting record (an existing chart for the same person, checked in the read-back), and the certified bundle must stop at the rule's check before the save with nothing written on every trial, or certification is withdrawn | On main | Unit tests; the OpenEMR fixture's verify.yaml declares the existing-duplicate rule | [QUALIFY_A_WORKFLOW.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/QUALIFY_A_WORKFLOW.md) |
| Right-record check before any write (structure, then OCR, then pixels) | Released | Real app and synthetic | [RESOLUTION_LADDER.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/RESOLUTION_LADDER.md), `runtime/identity.py` |
| Read the saved record back from the system of record (API, database, FHIR, separate session) | Released | Real app (OpenEMR 12 of 12 fields) | [VERIFICATION.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/VERIFICATION.md), `runtime/effects/` |
| Check a change that no app database holds: a saved file (contents and SHA-256), a Windows registry value (`winreg`, read-only) or a macOS preference key (`defaults export`), declared as typed sources in `verify.yaml` (`kind: local-state`); a missing value is a state, a failed read halts | On main | Real app in the lab: Windows 11 Notepad, recorded, compiled, replayed with a new note and checked by `verify-run` in the guest, 3 of 4 final trials `verified` (the fourth hit a lab timeout before replay), each with a skipped-replay control refuted; Windows registry reads checked on the same machine. The macOS source is unit-tested only | [LOCAL_STATE_CHECKS.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/LOCAL_STATE_CHECKS.md), `runtime/effects/local_state.py`, `examples/local_state/` |
| Generate read-only OS `local-state` verification contracts for built-in everyday tasks (`macos_night_shift` via private `CoreBrightness`, `windows_night_light` via `HKCU` CloudStore `Data` byte 18 heuristic, and `macos_calendar_event` via EventKit `EKEventStore` matching exact title, local-timezone start/end, recurrence, and optional `event_uid`), wired into `openadapt quickstart --task night-shift` and `--task calendar-block` (with opt-in `--probe-baseline` and withheld revert contract when baseline is unreadable); unreadable or unsupported hosts fail closed as `INDETERMINATE` | Experimental | Unit-tested across all 3 probes (enabled/disabled, malformed bytes, missing/ambiguous calendars, unauthorized EventKit, aware timezone conversion, wrong OS -> fail-closed `INDETERMINATE`) and contract generation; live Windows and end-to-end macOS toggle runs not yet recorded | `openadapt quickstart --task`, [LOCAL_STATE_CHECKS.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/LOCAL_STATE_CHECKS.md), `openadapt/quickstart/everyday.py`, `runtime/effects/local_state.py` |
| Read values out of an app as a workflow step (READ), with a records format, a signed review queue and export to CSV or a database | Released ([#1229](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1229), [#1215](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1215), [#1218](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1218)–[#1224](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1224)) | Synthetic (mock desktop apps) | `openadapt_flow/interchange/` |
| Stop before the effect instead of improvising (`HALTED_BEFORE_EFFECT`) | Released | Real app and synthetic | `runtime/replayer.py` |
| Fill a multi-step browser form or quote wizard from an intake record, stop for an operator on a prefill that disagrees with the intake or a question the intake does not answer (decided in a Chrome side panel), submit once, and give every typed, selected or kept field a read-back verdict: `passed`, `failed` or `not_checked`. A field it cannot read back is `not_checked`, never passed; such a submit ends `readback_incomplete` with no receipt | On main, prototype; not on PyPI until Flow 3.4.0 ([#2308](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/2308)) | Synthetic only. Four quote portals built separately from the layer, 32 scored cases, pre-registered: 6 correct submissions, 0 wrong values submitted, 0 verified (every field on the one workable portal is `not_checked`, because its summary is plain text). The surface cannot see iframe or shadow-DOM forms or fill type-aheads, so 3 of 4 portals submitted nothing. Estimator, session-timeout and type-ahead traps were never reached. Rule proposals from repeated operator answers (`form_tx/learning.py`) had no measured effect: none qualified ([RESULTS](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/benchmark/form_tx_heldout_run/RESULTS.md)) | `openadapt_flow/form_tx/`, [FORM_TX.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/FORM_TX.md) |
| Never retry an uncertain save (`RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED`) | Released | Synthetic (fault server) | [VERIFICATION.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/VERIFICATION.md) |
| One check-level scale, 0 to 5, from "unchecked" to "counterparty confirmed" | Released | Unit tests | `openadapt_flow/check_level.py` |
| One receipt word per check, the same on every path: `VERIFIED` only at level 3 (a separate session) or 4 (the system of record), always with the basis that produced the evidence (`separate_session`, `system_api`, `activity_log`, `db_frame` or `owned_connection`); `SHOWN` for an acting-screen re-read, `CONFIRMED` for the counterparty, `ATTESTED` for an operator and `RECORDED` for the rest. `VERIFIED` means "as of the read-back time the read-back showed this value", not "persisted". Run receipts (`record/run/v1`, an additive optional field), `verify-run` receipts and `tx` receipts carry an evidence-scope block: level, basis, word, the wire channel watched, the read-back time, the recheck window, and what it did not cover (always server-side async and outbound effects; a run receipt says it has no per-read time). A run receipt never says `VERIFIED` below level 3. Receipts without the block still verify. A `verify-run` contract with `minimum_effect_strength: independent_session` now verifies on a separate-session read | On main | Unit tests (parity across the runtime report, `verify-run`, `tx` and Execute v1; fake verifiers) | `openadapt_types/check_level.py`, `openadapt_types/evidence_scope.py`, `openadapt_flow/evidence_basis.py` |
| Grade a file, PDF or email check by who produced it: a file the acting session wrote or downloaded, or one with no declared producer, is at most `same_screen`; one a separate session fetched is at most `separate_session`; only a declared `system_of_record` producer reaches `system_of_record`. A store that overlaps the acting session's folders (named ones, the user's Downloads, a Playwright download folder) is graded as the acting session's whatever is declared. Under a strong declared producer, a scan that reads a file in a browser download folder beneath the store, or a symlink out of it, is refused as INDETERMINATE. | Commit one record update through a transaction lens: `openadapt-verify tx-run` (or `tx_verified` in Python) reads the target record, sends the update, reads it back and judges the intended fields and every other field (frame) with one comparison policy, and signs a receipt. Without a separately supplied SQLite row authority every HTTP write is refused; `--prototype-unqualified` runs it with no automatic undo, and its result is `UNCERTAIN` unless the read-back is a cache-bypassed API read whose record version is exactly one past the before-image's, which is `CONFIRMED` with basis `system_api`. `tx-induce` proposes a lens from a HAR trace and can probe a declared sandbox, but its probe report never authorizes execution, and an observed mismatch never becomes an accepted value mapping. Induction takes route roles from what each request did, so a create sent as `PUT` and an update sent as `POST` are recognized, and the sandbox probe checks an update route of any method for replace semantics. A field that only looks like a timestamp stays in the frame unless the probe sees the server change it. Induction refuses a trace that shows no write it can attribute to a record (an update at the record's URL, or a create whose record is then read there) instead of guessing a route; the CLI allows a guessed item route only when it certifies the lens on a sandbox. When the probe cannot create its own record, an update lens is left in replace mode (whole-record writes), and a certification fault the server refuses is reported as not delivered, never as a pass. Undo refuses to overwrite a change made after the write. The wire tap hands a redirect that stays on the tapped origin back to the client and refuses one that leaves it; it never follows a redirect itself. A field the server is seen rewriting between `NULL` and `""` gets a `null_empty` codec, learned per field by the probe or from the trace, so that change alone is not a clobber; any other change on the field still is. The wire tap counts a GraphQL query (on `/graphql` or `/$graphql`) and a batch of `GET`s as reads. Another `POST` counts as a read only when it matches a read route declared as data; `probe_read_routes` learns those by replaying a trace on a sandbox reset to its pre-trace state and requiring that a whole-store digest not change. An app whose calls all go to one RPC endpoint gets a lens whose read and write carry their arguments in the body (`body_template`), whose record is found at a path such as `result.0`, and whose 2xx answer with an `error` member counts as a failed call; induction learns it from a read that returns the named records and a write that a later read confirms, and reads back the fields the trace itself read. Not checked: server-side effects outside the target record, such as triggers or background jobs | On main ([#2293](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/2293)) | Synthetic (local SQLite and HTTP fixture servers), plus induction and the replace probe on one open-source task app (recorded trace in CI, live tests in the lab) | `openadapt-verify tx-induce`, `tx-run`, `openadapt_flow/tx/`, `openadapt_verify/tx.py` |
| Verify a write to an API or SaaS system with no database to diff: `openadapt proxy --api systems.tx.yaml` serves `api_read` and `api_write` beside the SQL tools on the same MCP endpoint and keeps the API credentials out of the agent's environment. Each write is sent once under a key derived from the task and the record, never the payload. A retry returns the first result, a regenerated payload is refused, and a crash between the send and the ledger is recovered by finding the write. The key goes out as `Idempotency-Key` where the API honors one, or as a FHIR conditional create. The record is then read back and judged with the tx codecs, including `null_empty`. The system's own event or audit log is read from an id-placed cursor, and the write's own event must appear with no other resource changed by the same credentials. A FHIR `AuditEvent` search, an event stream and a REST activity feed are all declared as data in the tx file. Every outcome gets a `record/run/v1` receipt. Scope is the resource and the actor: changes by other callers, and changes the log doesn't record, aren't checked. A whole-record (`replace`) update or a delete over another caller's edit is refused by the server when the route declares a `precondition` (`If-Match` from the read's `ETag` or a version field) with enforcement evidence: a probe recorded in the pack, or one the adapter runs once per route. Without a precondition it is never `VERIFIED`, only `COMPLETED_UNVERIFIED` (`unconditional_write`; `precondition_unproven` without evidence), and `api_write` reports it as an error. A retry that returns a stored result is capped the same way | [#2437](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/2437), stacked on [#2428](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/2428) | Real apps (Medplum 5.2.8 `AuditEvent`, Gitea 1.24.6 activity feed, synthetic data): 0 of 400 clean writes stopped on each; Medplum rerun with its `If-Match` probe recorded in the pack, 400 of 400 `VERIFIED`. Every planted fault the log exposes was stopped: wrong value, duplicate, partial write and same-actor collateral change, 50 of 50 per class, except that on Medplum a duplicate update no longer lands (the server refused all 50 second PUTs with 412). Known misses: a collateral title edit on Gitea, which its feed doesn't record (0 of 50 stopped), and another caller's change on either system (0 of 50). 50 of 50 regenerated-payload retries were refused on each. Stripe not run (no test-mode key) | [API_VERIFICATION.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/API_VERIFICATION.md), [benchmark/api_scoped](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/benchmark/api_scoped/RESULTS.md), `openadapt_flow/txplan/scoped.py`, `openadapt_flow/txplan/audit.py` |
| Reconcile one prior authorization or claim across the EHR (FHIR), the clearinghouse (X12 278 and 277 files) and the payer (Da Vinci PAS): each leg is a verifier contract judged by the same record checks, and the result names each break (`not_received`, `mismatch`, `not_written_back`, `duplicate`, `not_accepted`) with `CONFIRMED`/`REFUTED`/`UNCERTAIN` and a Scope; absence before a deadline is `UNCERTAIN`, an unreadable store is never agreement, a rejected or returned 277 is never agreement, and a judged record or value with two distinct candidates in the read (repeated segments, list elements, join targets, a group's latest) is never `CONFIRMED` | On main | HL7 Da Vinci PAS reference implementation and Medplum run locally, synthetic X12: 36 of 36 planted breaks found, 0 of 27 faulty units `CONFIRMED`, 17 of 17 clean units `CONFIRMED` (units 1 to 47; the 3 status-category units added later are covered by unit tests); a Hypothesis property test over generated multi-candidate reads; Epic's public sandbox read-only as the EHR leg | `openadapt-flow reconcile`, [RECONCILE.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/RECONCILE.md), [results](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/benchmark/reconcile/RESULTS.md) |
| Catch a write that lands after the verdict (a background job, a trigger, a delayed side record): a `CONFIRMED` with a recheck due is provisional (`provisional`, `recheck_due_at`); the recheck reads the whole database again and refutes the earlier result when a change since the post-save read has no explanation, and a recheck that doesn't confirm holds the write in the ledger. Run it from Python (`verifier.recheck`) or MCP (`verify_recheck`). A write after the recheck's read is not seen (`frame.database.recheck_after_s`, no default window) | Released ([#1639](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1639)); provisional result, MCP tool and ledger hold ([#1669](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1669)) | Real app (Dolibarr 21 and EspoCRM 10 on MariaDB 11.4, 180 s window: 4 of 4 planted late writes at 125 to 130 s refuted at the recheck, correct writes confirmed; EspoCRM's cron daemon needs its job tables declared; Redmine 6.1 on PostgreSQL 17, 180 s window: the first-contact study's late writes F19 and F20 refuted at the recheck, correct writes confirmed); synthetic (SQLite); opt-in live OpenEMR test | `openadapt_flow/verifier.py`, `runtime/effects/late_write.py`, [VERIFY_RUN.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/VERIFY_RUN.md#writes-that-land-later) |
| Recheck a write to a system with no database access, after a window the caller sets: `runtime/effects/api_recheck.py` takes the system's log checkpoint, then reads the record through its API (a REST, FHIR or GraphQL verifier, through `VerifierReadback`; FHIR and GraphQL need a named server version, and a redacting verifier is refused), keeping only MACs of the record's identity, declared fields and version, keyed by the salt and this host's frame secret. At or after the due time it reads both again. `VERIFIED` means only that, between the start and end of the recheck, the read-back showed the same record and values and, when a log was read, the log since the checkpoint showed no unexplained change. Without a log the basis is the API read-back alone, and the result lists this caller's changes to other records as not covered. This caller's own unexplained entry in the log is `REFUTED`, and so is a changed or deleted record that the log doesn't attribute to another or an unknown actor. These are `NOT_CHECKED`: another actor's or an unknown entry's change; a read-back that lands on a different record or matches more than one; an exempted entry whose author or operation disagrees; a version that moved while the values stayed the same; a log read that didn't reach the checkpoint; a state that doesn't match its receipt; an early recheck; and a first result that wasn't verified. Entry ids decide what is in the window, never clock times. Every result lists what it didn't cover, including server-side async and outbound effects. Not yet: the log reader (the activity log adapter is a protocol; a reader for a system's own audit or event log is not on main), the receipt field, and an MCP tool | On main ([#2472](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/2472)) | Synthetic (scripted log and record; MockMed's REST server over real HTTP: a late note edit refuted, a change to an undeclared field not checked) | `openadapt_flow/runtime/effects/api_recheck.py` |
| Diff the whole database for the frame (`frame.database`) on SQLite, MySQL, MariaDB and PostgreSQL. On MySQL and MariaDB every column type is read exactly (binary strings, `BIT`, geometries and vectors as hex, `FLOAT` widened to `DOUBLE`, `JSON` as stored text, decimals at full precision). On PostgreSQL every column type is read as text by a declared rule in a session pinned to UTC and exact float output, and a type without a rule, a table the account can't read in full, or an unreadable sequence is refused. So a row the save adds, changes or removes outside the declared records, such as an extra planned call or a stream note, is refuted unless a declared effect, a side record, an attributed concurrent write or an allow-listed bookkeeping table explains it | Released ([#1661](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1661)); PostgreSQL ([#1673](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1673)) | Real app (Dolibarr 21 on MariaDB 11.4: all 387 tables read where the frame raised `TypeError`; EspoCRM on MariaDB 11.4: the first-contact study's extra call and stream note refuted, correct opportunities verified; Redmine 6.1 on PostgreSQL 17: 58 tables read, a stray upload in a table the contract doesn't read refuted, correct writes verified); live MariaDB and PostgreSQL type tests | [VERIFY_RUN.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/VERIFY_RUN.md#the-whole-database), `runtime/effects/db_snapshot.py` |
| Learn, then enforce: excuse the app's own per-request writes on the acting user's own rows (the user's `last_login`, a token's `last_seen`, a first-login row) that make the whole-database frame refute every correct write. `learn collect` records each check's moved rows and the agent's request-body field names from a shadow run; `learn propose` proposes only moves on the acting user's rows (users table named once, user columns from the schema's foreign keys), never a column the agent sent or the contract names, as an exact column set seen in 3 of every 5 checks; one `learn approve` by a person writes `frame.learned` with the proposal's digest. At check time the relation is derived again from the run's actor: never another user's row, another column, a removal, more added rows than learned, or a row added for someone else. Collateral on the written row is never learned (a `relation: target` entry is refused at load); the generator's bookkeeping answer excuses those columns. Not yet: tables over `max_rows` | [#1679](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1679) | Real app (three held-out apps on MariaDB and PostgreSQL, replayed agent writes: correct writes of the kinds with an approved excuse confirmed 0 -> 74 of 100, the rest stopped at begin or by app rows that are neither the write's nor the actor's; 0 of 42 planted harms passed); adversarial tests on SQLite, MySQL and PostgreSQL | `openadapt-flow learn`, [LEARNED_EXCUSES.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/LEARNED_EXCUSES.md) |
| Learn per-request bookkeeping from read-only requests, with no approval: `learn probe` reads the whole-database frame of one contract, sends only GET and HEAD requests as the agent, and reads again; a changed row of the acting user that every round (at least two) shows (users table derived from the manifest's actor parameters by foreign key) becomes a `frame.learned` excuse with `source: read_only_probe`, exact columns only, never a column the probe, the parameters or a contract names. Added rows, other users' rows and rows no user owns are not admitted (added rows are listed for `learn approve`), and only contracts whose every effect creates new records, or that read the target's versions on every other effect's surface, get the excuses (an update with no version source can't see a lost update without the bookkeeping move). Not yet: background rows that move with no request, derived rows a write recomputes | (this PR) | Real app replay (first-contact retest, four apps, frozen vs `main` vs this branch on identical writes): correct writes stopped on the app with per-user last-login bookkeeping 77 -> 36 of 77, in-scope harms 26 of 26 stopped before and after; on a second app 46 -> 34 of 46 replayed agent writes, its three lost updates still stopped; no change on two apps without such bookkeeping and on two held-out apps (the probe learned nothing there). One out-of-scope late duplicate that bookkeeping used to mask now passes; adversarial tests on SQLite, MySQL and PostgreSQL | `openadapt-flow learn probe`, [LEARNED_EXCUSES.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/LEARNED_EXCUSES.md) |
| Count who saved an update's target on PostgreSQL, so learned bookkeeping can be excused on updates and found checks too: `frame.row_versions` holds a read-only REPEATABLE READ snapshot from the baseline to the judge; the replaced row version's `xmax` against the current row's `xmin` says whether one transaction or more wrote the target. Two or more refute the frame as a lost update; a judge in another process, a failed read, a target created in the window, an `xmax` that could be a shared lock naming another updater, or a `frame.row_versions` table and key that aren't the ones the target surface reads the target from stop it as not checked. `learn probe --apply` writes the source beside the excuse when the contract's read is one `SELECT` over one table (no join, `UNION`, subquery or second statement). Not yet: MySQL and MariaDB targets (a last-saved marker can't count saves; they need a history read or the change log), rows a window adds and removes on a composite key | (this PR) | Real app replay (InvenTree on PostgreSQL, first-contact retest, frozen vs fix vs this branch on identical writes): correct writes stopped 65, 48 and 27 of 65; the 21 released were all bookkeeping stops on updates and found checks, and none newly stopped; 0 of 31 planted and agent harms passed in any variant, and the row-version check itself refuted the planted lost updates (the pack's 2 plus a no-gap PATCH, a no-gap PUT, a found-check revert and a child-row revert); 9 of 9 excuse attacks stopped. No change on MariaDB apps (no source is derived) | `openadapt-flow learn probe`, [LEARNED_EXCUSES.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/LEARNED_EXCUSES.md) |
| Catch a lost update: another user saves a change to the record while the agent works, and the agent saves its stale copy over it. Before and after look like a correct update, so `frame.versions` reads the target's versions (FHIR or SQL version history, a version column, or the app's audit or action-history table) before and after the write. ## Branching work, not one linear path

| Capability | Status | Evidence | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Learn one program with branches from two or more recordings, or say which recordings are missing | Released | Synthetic | `openadapt-flow induce`, `disambiguate`; [CAPABILITIES.md (flow)](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/CAPABILITIES.md) |
| Learn a guarded branch from several halts fixed the same way | Released | Synthetic | `openadapt-flow teach-branch`, `learning/branch_teach.py` |
| Run a program over a worklist | Released | Real app | `openadapt-flow for-each` |
| Learn a worklist loop from recordings that search a record, open it, work it and go back to the list, even when the last row skips the return or rows differ (a field some rows lack, a write some rows get behind a screen check a person accepts). Each pass selects the row's own record by its values, verifies it, and checks that row's write. Certified and governed runs refuse it until qualification covers it | Released ([#1435](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1435)) | Synthetic (held-out rows run through the interpreter against an in-memory app) | `openadapt-flow induce`; `Step.target_param` |
| Score whether a program generalizes by running held-out items: each item runs through the replayer with its own inputs and record check, and an independent check the program never sees says whether the intended record got exactly the intended change (generalized, halted safely, silent wrong, wrong effect, unconfirmed write); a loop program runs each item as a one-row worklist. `induce --held-out` stays a structural shape check that runs nothing | Released ([#1527](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1527)) | Synthetic (an induced worklist loop scored on held-out rows against an in-memory chart app) | `openadapt_flow.validation.behavioral_generalization` |
| Typed business decisions inside a run | Released | Synthetic | `business_decision` states, `openadapt-flow business-decisions` |
| Watch many real runs in the background and mine candidate branches (shadow mode) | Released ([#1212](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1212)) | Synthetic | [SHADOW_MINING.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/capture/docs/SHADOW_MINING.md), [LEARN_FROM_MANY_RUNS.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/LEARN_FROM_MANY_RUNS.md) |
| Fill a workflow's inputs from a referral PDF, fax image or email | Released | Synthetic | `openadapt-flow intake`, [INTAKE.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/INTAKE.md) |
| Use spoken narration while recording to propose the rule behind a branch | Released ([#1291](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1291)) | Synthetic (generated audio) | `openadapt-capture[audio,privacy]` |
| Settle a disagreement between recordings by trying both paths on a test copy of the app and reading the record back | Released ([#1276](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1276), [#1289](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1289)) | Synthetic (MockMed; desktop and remote test copies) | `induce --probe-on` |
| Route each item to the right verified variant of a program | Released ([#1264](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1264)) | Synthetic | `variants`, `route` |
