## The fastest layer the app allows

| Capability | Status | Evidence | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Page structure (DOM, UI Automation, Accessibility) first, then template, OCR and geometry | Released | Real apps on the web; synthetic on Windows and macOS | [RESOLUTION_LADDER.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/RESOLUTION_LADDER.md) |
| Run a step as a direct API call (`ApiActuator`, `ApiBinding`) | Released, hand-authored bindings | Synthetic benchmarks | `runtime/actuators/api.py` |
| Capture a recording's network traffic and compile a clean save into an API step, with the same record check | Released ([#1269](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1269)) | Synthetic patients on a local OpenEMR test copy | network capture, `ApiBinding` |
| Keep captured bodies off disk: `network.jsonl` and saved wire-tap HARs keep only declared field values (a recording's `--param` and `--identifier` fields; a wire policy's id and version fields) and a per-capture keyed hash of everything else, including URL query values; HTML, text and binary bodies keep only size and hash, taken from the bytes as sent (only a body labelled JSON, or with no content type, is parsed as JSON); the recording's `app_url` query and URL-valued HAR headers are minimized too, and a HAR marked minimized that carries a raw body is refused on load. Raw bodies (`--capture-network-bodies raw`, `save_har(raw_bodies=True)`), which API step proposals need, are refused unless sealed at rest or plaintext is explicitly allowed (`OPENADAPT_FLOW_PLAINTEXT_AT_REST`, warned and logged). Not covered: URL path segments and header values beyond credential redaction | On main (this PR) | Synthetic PHI in request and response bodies, absent from every file after decryption in raw, percent, JSON-escaped, base64 and gzip forms; positive controls with raw | `openadapt_flow/capture_privacy.py`, [NETWORK_CAPTURE.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/NETWORK_CAPTURE.md#bodies-minimized-by-default) |
| Fall back from the API step to page structure when the API is unavailable, before anything is sent | Released ([#1269](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1269)) | Synthetic | [#1269](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1269) |
| Run a form's own script before an API save instead of refusing the form: field handlers, `onsubmit`, submit listeners and custom validate.js rules (OpenEMR's `pastDate`) run on the run's values in a scratch copy of the session with every write blocked, and the save is sent only when the page lets the submit through and would send the same body | On main | Synthetic (headless Chromium against a local test page) | [API_TIER.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/API_TIER.md#what-happens-at-run-time), `runtime/actuators/form_eval.py` |
| Compare paired GUI/API database changes with `api admit --footprint`: changed rows retain their identity and before/after values, and unexplained field differences refuse. Variation alone does not establish server ownership. | This PR | Synthetic headless Chromium and SQLite; generated insert ID/time differences conservatively refuse | `openadapt_flow/api_footprint.py` |
| Propose API steps for saves a page's script sends as JSON or as a GraphQL mutation: each typed value bound to its one JSON leaf, constants sent as recorded, values the page makes on each save refused, the app's own auth headers reused from the live session in memory only, and a GraphQL answer with errors halts | This PR | Headless Chromium against a local single-page app; EspoCRM, Medplum and Wiki.js fixtures | [API_TIER.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/API_TIER.md#json-and-graphql-saves) |
| Propose API steps for more save shapes: multipart saves with no file (encoded as Chromium encodes them), the clicked submit button's `name=value`, empty file inputs, forms with no `action`, and saves the page's script sends to another endpoint (run through the page's own script before every save); success addresses keep a record's path with numbers and hashes generalized | This PR | Headless Chromium against local test pages, and recordings from Redmine, WordPress, NetBox, Dolibarr and Trac fixtures | [API_TIER.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/API_TIER.md#what-the-compiler-checks) |
| Declare the other writes in an API step's span as an ordered sequence: the page's own background requests (another document's script, loaded before the form, to an endpoint the form doesn't name) are listed and not sent; a write a step caused is sent in its recorded place before the save, read back by that step's record check, and a failure stops the run with nothing after it sent and nothing retried | On main | Synthetic | [API_TIER.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/API_TIER.md#other-writes-in-the-span) |
| Approve an API step's exact request under per-item approval: one digest binds the request bytes, the record and the record check, and a changed request is not sent | Released ([#1355](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1355)) | Synthetic | [API_TIER.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/API_TIER.md#under-an-approval-mode) |
| Run an API step in a durable run: checkpoint the span after the save is sent, never resend or redo a save that may have landed, and reconcile it by reading the record back | Released ([#1358](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1358)) | Synthetic | [API_TIER.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/API_TIER.md#in-a-durable-run) |
| Run an admitted API step under a governed run authorization and the Standard or Regulated profile: the authorization names the API step by digest, the person who admits it names the right-record parameter, and the outcome reads `VERIFIED` | Released ([#1361](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1361)) | Synthetic | [API_TIER.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/API_TIER.md#under-governance) |
| Run an admitted API step under a managed (Cloud) dispatch whose authorization names it: the API step rows are inside the dispatch digest Cloud signs, and each send still needs Cloud's delivery permit | On main | Synthetic | [API_TIER.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/API_TIER.md#under-governance) |

## When the app changes

| Capability | Status | Evidence | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Governed repair: propose, review, campaigns, approval, staging, canary, rollback | Released | Synthetic | `openadapt-flow repair`, [REPAIR_LIFECYCLE.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/REPAIR_LIFECYCLE.md) |
| A calling agent demonstrates the fix for a halted run; the result is a repair candidate | Released (2.1.0) | Synthetic | `run --hold-on-halt`, `repair/agent_teach.py` |
| Font and layout drift halts with a named reason | Released | Synthetic | `runtime/layout_drift.py` |
| Self-repair: an agent proposes a fix for one halted click, Flow probes it up to the save without saving, a person approves | Released ([#1265](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1265)) | Synthetic (MockMed redesign) | `run --self-repair`, [#1265](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1265) |
| A scroll that never finds the next click's target halts on that click, so self-repair can take a relabelled control behind a scroll; the refusal for unreviewed-risk steps names them | Released ([#1337](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1337)) | Synthetic; openIMIS drift row checked offline on its recorded frames | `runtime/replayer.py`, `qualify set-risk` |

| Opt-in fallback from a wrapped task's compiled program to the agent on drift: only when the hold is a terminal halt whose report is `HALTED_BEFORE_EFFECT` with no step needing reconciliation, bound to the admitted bundle, with zero replay model calls and a record check whose reads both succeeded and found no change. Never on `RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED`, a lost reply, `RECORD_CHECK_FAILED`, an unreadable system of record or a receipt that is not `VERIFIED`. The agent is built only once a fallback may start and runs through compile-agent's harness (right-record check, origin fence, read-back) with a person approving each save at a pre-commit gate (the terminal, or a signed item approval from a paired phone or `openadapt-flow item-approval approve`) and its own spend cap. A fallback is `VERIFIED` only when the final task-scoped read confirms the save; otherwise it is `RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED` with both readings kept. Its draft is never admitted, and a verified run opens a repair candidate for a person to approve. The default stays the hold. `openadapt-flow wrap-dispatch` runs only the admitted program (a miss runs nothing), stores the whole result with the request, and exposes the hold (`status`, `release`, `evict`); release refuses a fallback that is still running | Experimental, this PR | Synthetic: unit tests on the real cache, hold, report and item-approval checks (answers signed with a test approver key on a real roster, through the decision portal's functions and the `item-approval approve` command); MockMed in headless Chromium with a scripted fallback agent, program run in-process ([benchmark/wrap_fallback](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/benchmark/wrap_fallback/README.md)). | Agent-to-agent handoffs: when one agent hands a result to another, the run's signed receipt (`record/run/v1`) goes with it (`openadapt handoff send`, inline, detached beside a file, or POSTed to a webhook), and the receiver checks it against keys it pins (`openadapt handoff verify`). The verdict gives the signer role from the receiver's registry, integrity, checks passed and not checked, and "confirmed in the other party's system" lines; it always says a valid signature proves who signed, not that the claim is true, binds the payload as the receipt's `payload` subject (re-signed by the run's own key; other bytes or no payload subject are refused), and counts a confirmation as independent only when it was read from the other party's system. | Score a candidate before it saves anything: `openadapt-flow readiness` imports 20 to 50 tasks a person did (the save from the browser recording's network capture, else a read-back through the verify config's reader, else refused), runs the candidate agent (`--agent-cmd`) or compiled program (`--program`) on each task in its own headless browser (DevTools on a pipe only, reached through a loopback relay that refuses any request without the run's random token; the page can reach only the app's origins) where the shadow hold refuses every non-GET request to the app origin (autosaves, drafts and locks included) after recording the write it would have made, and a browser-level hold hands every request of every other tab, popup, browser context and worker to the same hold (a write from one of them makes the case `NOT_CHECKED`, reason `extra_target`, and `scope_ok` false). | Publish a wrapped task as a hosted endpoint with one credential: `openadapt wrap publish --task TASK` uses only `OPENADAPT_API_KEY`. It finds the task's admitted program, re-verifies its admission signature, refuses a held task, a program without a read-back check (no saving step, a save with no effect contract, or no confirmed `verify.yaml`), symbolic links and a non-public app URL, and stages the bundle with its read-back configuration. It sanitizes the bundle and the recording it was compiled from (the generated wrap files declare each field as content, always scrubbed, or structural, kept only with its machine shape, so schema ids, step ids, digests and the signed admission survive the scrub byte-for-byte), shows one summary and asks once (`--yes` for scripts), finds the key's organization (`GET /api/v1/whoami`, or `--org`), registers the local admission public key with it once, attests the program from the wrap run's own signed recording and attended canary (strict lint with no warn or error finding, certification, VERIFIED replay) against a challenge from the organization's API-key route, uploads it through the governed bundle push to `POST /api/v1/org/{org}/workflow` (or `PUT .../workflow/{id}/definition`), then reads the Cloud workflow definition and prints the endpoint URL and `curl` examples from the acknowledged `execute_path` and `qualification_id`. Each refusal is one line with a code. The upload carries the program's value-free Standard run shape. A managed run of the program rests on its signed admission: `openadapt-flow run --managed-dispatch-file` checks the admission against the registered admission key, requires the authorization to name that admission and match the shape, and reads back through the bundled `verify.yaml`. The CLI, public runtime and deployment API carry one-use verification bound to that dispatch's admission, bundle, inputs, policy, run, session and current trust registry; resume verifies a fresh proof. Each input checks that scope again after preparation and requires a signed v3 permit with a receiver-checked exclusive start deadline. API sequences acknowledge every request separately. Missing receipts or late completion evidence halt further input and require reconciliation. Publish refuses, before anything is uploaded, an admission mode a hosted run cannot verify (only a person's admission or a registered CI admitter key), and an admitter-key admission whose key the organization has not registered (`GET /api/v1/org/{org}/admitter-keys`). The recording stays on the machine; only its sanitized hash is attested. Regulated is refused (`openadapt_flow.jit.hosted_authority`) | On main | Unit tests (real bundle, record check, staging, local sanitization and signed wrap evidence; the attestation's recording binding checked on real derivatives; the whoami, admission-key, challenge, workflow upload and definition routes mocked at the HTTP boundary); no run against a live Cloud deployment. Relies on the API-key workflow routes in openadapt-cloud#430 (merged 2026-11-14), which accept this v2 attestation only behind a flag that is off by default; the whoami route is not in #430 yet | `openadapt_flow.wrap.publish`, [WRAP_PUBLISH.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/WRAP_PUBLISH.md), `packages/flow/tests/test_wrap_publish.py`, `packages/flow/tests/test_jit_hosted_authority.py`, `packages/flow/tests/test_jit_hosted_managed_replay.py` |
| Try `openadapt wrap` with one command: `uvx --python 3.12 'openadapt[wrap]@latest' wrap --example` (the `wrap` extra brings the agent SDK; the base launcher leaves it out) starts a bundled synthetic clinic app (MockMed) on 127.0.0.1, has OpenAdapt's built-in Claude agent save one note in a headless browser, reads the save back, compiles the run, runs a canary, and admits it with a throwaway key made in the example's own folder (the proposed checks are confirmed automatically, which only a synthetic app allows). Then a new note runs the compiled program over its emitted MCP server with no model calls, and it prints the app's record and the cost of both runs. It needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (or `OPENAI_API_KEY` with `--provider openai`, `--model` and reviewed `--price` values); the task is packaged data (`openadapt_flow/wrap/examples/`). Because the data is synthetic, screenshots go to the model unscrubbed under the recorded opt-out. | Wrapped tasks that sign in: during `openadapt wrap`'s first run the recorder finds a password field (`type=password`, or `autocomplete` `current-password`/`new-password`) and the username field paired with it (`autocomplete=username`, or a unique text, email or phone candidate paired across all password controls in the composed form; ambiguous or unreadable controls refuse declared inputs) from the page's markup alone. Automatic withholding requires that observation seam; a missing or noncallable seam refuses before capture or actor entry. Screen-only native backends use the existing explicit person-secret handoff instead of this automatic path. Their inputs become secret parameters: the recording, program, run records, receipts and publish upload keep the name and never the value, the observed field regions are blacked out in recording frames (arbitrary field movement or echoes are not proven redacted), a credential field given text that matches no declared input is refused before typing, a form with exactly a username and current password is classified as sign-in without lowering independent keyword risk, and replay run screenshots contain black frames while checks use the original pixels in memory, and no compiled pixel check covers a withheld field's black box (it is clipped clear of it or dropped). Secret environment/vault aliases must be unambiguous, and managed params files cannot supply secret values. The canary and cached runs type them from `OPENADAPT_FLOW_SECRET_<NAME>`, set from memory for one run; `publish` lists them as `secret_parameters`, outside the call's inputs | On main ([#2294](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/2294), merged 2026-11-20) | Synthetic (a sign-in notes app in headless Chromium through the real wrap path: first run, canary, admission, publish staging, and a cached run under mcp 2, with a byte scan for the values in every file; unit tests with a fake backend for detection, frame redaction, refusals and the sign-in submit rule). Genuine RDP/Citrix backends refuse automatic withholding before input; explicit person-secret handoff remains tested. | Sign-ins with a second factor: a `second_factor` step (`code` for a text-message, email or authenticator code, `approval` for a push approval) waits for a person when it runs, through the runner's control plane, a local command, or the run's own terminal when it has one (on a POSIX terminal or the Windows console; the code is never echoed, and normal input comes back however the read ends). Before anyone is asked, the focused field must be an empty `autocomplete="one-time-code"` input and the page draws it as dots; after the answer the same field must still have focus and be empty. The code is filled once into that element (a field split into one box per character is refused), never retried, and never stored, logged, shown to a model or drawn on screen. No source, a late or malformed answer, a decline, a field that changed, or a backend that can't bind the field stops the step before typing with a closed `second_factor_*` code; an older runtime refuses the bundle. | Guard an agent you already run: attach to its own Chromium over CDP (one added line), hold each save until the record on screen is the one the task names, block it and tell the agent why when it isn't, read the save back; a run that reads back correctly becomes a draft program with a record check from scaffold-verifier, which a person confirms and admits, then a `taught_*` tool with no model calls. `--observe-only` never blocks. | Flight recorder for an agent you already run: `openadapt flight -- CMD` puts a loopback proxy in front of the model API the agent calls (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `OPENAI_BASE_URL`), meters and prices each call (an unpriced model's cost is recorded as unknown), honours a `--max-cost-usd` cap and logs each computer action. Scrubbing: the strings in the request (message text, tool-call arguments, tool results, URLs cut to their origin) and the screenshots it recognises (PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP, TIFF, WEBP) are scrubbed before they are sent (see "What the scrubber does not cover" in FLIGHT_RECORDER.md); a request that can't be scrubbed is answered 502 and never sent, and the run refuses to start when openadapt-privacy, its spaCy model or tesseract is missing. Each value becomes a run token (`[PERSON_1]`, the same in text and on screen, painted over with the token written in); tokens in tool-call inputs are turned back into the real values before the response reaches the agent, so it can type them; the map stays local (`pseudonyms.json`, 0600). Measured on 50 synthetic records: 97.6 to 98.0% of fields in text and 97.2% in rendered screenshots, every miss a name; 93.1% of non-personal words on a synthetic work-list screen stay readable (30.9% with Presidio's image redaction). The agent still can't read a name it must check; task success with scrubbing on is not measured. The scrubber covers ordinary agent traffic in standard encodings (base64 in any wrapping, JSON escapes; image signatures are searched across the whole request and dense base64-like text refuses, per string and across the request). Images are recognised and scrubbed in PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP, TIFF and WEBP; other image formats are refused only when the density backstops catch them, and a page with text on a flat background, uncompressed in another format, can get through; the backstops can refuse ordinary content that looks encoded (git SHAs, many camelCase identifiers, random tokens), and because the history is resent a refused turn refuses the rest of the run; an agent that deliberately re-encodes data (hex, percent-encoding, a custom scheme) can get it past the scrubber, so a hostile agent is out of scope and the egress block and provider choice are the controls there. Egress: on macOS the agent runs under `sandbox-exec` with outbound network denied except loopback; elsewhere `flight` refuses to run unless `--allow-unenforced-egress` is given (recorded). A run whose agent reports more model calls than the proxy saw, or that tried a direct call through the proxy variables, exits 3 and is marked refused; a kernel-blocked connection is blocked but not counted. Python API: `openadapt_flow.flight.egress.ScrubbedEgress`. Gate: a one-line executor swap (`GatedComputer` for the Anthropic computer tool, `GatedComputerCall` for an OpenAI `computer_call` loop) holds every action not known to be safe: a click or drag passes only on focus/view roles or a short list of labels (Cancel, Close, Back, Search, Open...; non-English and unreadable labels are held; OCR names a target only with text inside it); keys pass only on a short navigation list, or for editing inside a known text field; typing passes only when focus is known to be in a text field (from the accessibility hook, or the last click landed on one), and typed text with any control character is held; a focus move followed by more input in one action, Ctrl/Cmd+S, Ctrl/Cmd+Enter and any unknown action are held for a person (terminal y/N, or an item-approval request Desktop or a phone answers). It sees clicks and keys, not autosave. Writes `flight.json` (`openadapt.flight-run/v1`), `egress.json`, a scrubbed timeline and `timeline.html`. Image scrubbing covers text in the image, not faces | Experimental, PR [#2493](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/2493) | Synthetic (fake provider, scripted agent loop on MockMed in headless Chromium under the macOS egress block, the real Presidio scrubber on a 50-record synthetic PHI corpus ([recall](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/benchmark/flight/scrub_recall/README.md))); one real Claude run whose Save click was held, recorded before the scrubbing and gate changes ([flight](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/benchmark/flight/README.md)) | `openadapt-flow flight`, `openadapt_flow.flight`, [FLIGHT_RECORDER.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/FLIGHT_RECORDER.md) |
| Check a coding agent's writes to declared systems of record: `openadapt hooks install --agent claude-code` (or `codex`) writes project-local hooks (Claude Code `PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse`/`PostToolUseFailure`/`Stop`, Codex `PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse`/`Stop`). For a call that writes to a database, HTTP API or MCP tool declared in `openadapt.systems.yaml`, the pre-check allows, asks or blocks it by the write's approval mode (Codex can't ask from a hook, so `ask` is a deny until `openadapt hooks approve`); an undeclared write to a declared system is blocked or asked about; the read-back uses the verifier's contract (`openadapt.verify/v1`), a failed read-back is `UNCERTAIN` and the same call is then held; every outcome gets a signed `record/run/v1` receipt. Advisory: hooks see tool calls, so an agent with its own credentials and shell can bypass them; `--strict` (credential broker) is refused until a broker exists for these systems | Experimental, PR [#2411](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/2411) | Synthetic (a scripted harness sends each agent's documented hook input to the installed hook command; one run of live headless Claude Code 2.1.305 and Codex CLI 0.144.4 sessions, both against a local SQLite file and HTTP API: declared writes VERIFIED, an out-of-scope delete blocked, a broken read-back UNCERTAIN, and a Python write that builds the path at run time not seen, [hooks_live](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/benchmark/hooks_live/README.md)) | `openadapt hooks`, `openadapt_flow/hooks/`, [HOOKS.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/HOOKS.md) |
| Hold the database credentials and give the agent scoped tools: `openadapt proxy --postgres URL -- claude` (or `--sqlite`) serves an MCP endpoint on loopback with a per-run token and takes the credentials out of the agent's environment. Each SQL write is dry-run in a rolled-back transaction with its exact row-level diff (triggers and cascades included), approved by policy (`--auto-approve-max-rows`) or by a person (`y`, `openadapt plan approve`) against the plan digest, used once, committed only if its diff matches the plan, read back, and undone from its row images with a read-back proof. A regenerated statement over rows already written in the task is held for a person (`possible_replay`). Each stage gets a signed `record/run/v1` receipt with the approval block. The dry run covers effects inside the database only, and a write is `VERIFIED` only when the catalog shows nothing that could write outside the frame (foreign tables, rules, triggers, user functions or types, `TRUNCATE` and other DDL); otherwise it is capped at `COMPLETED_UNVERIFIED`. The lab counts were measured before that inventory existed | Experimental, this PR | Lab: PostgreSQL 16, 120 statements of 8 kinds, 0 missed effects, 0 false diffs, 120/120 verified undos, 0/20 regenerated statements applied (control 20/20 doubled), the independent `capture_database` read-back agreed on 120/120, 8-12 s from empty venv to first diff; one real MCP SDK session; one live headless Claude Code session (held, then applied and undone) | `openadapt proxy`, `openadapt_flow/txplan/proxy.py`, [TRANSACTIONS.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/TRANSACTIONS.md) |
| Dry-run, apply, undo and release a batch of writes to external systems: `openadapt plan create/approve/apply/undo/release/cancel` over an `openadapt.tx.yaml` of REST collections, SQL tables and mail. The diff comes from a staged transaction (SQL), a computed shadow with declared server-set and derived fields (REST) or the holdback queue (email). Approval is single-use and bound to the plan digest, a stale plan is refused, each write's idempotency key comes from the task and the record slot (never the payload), and a retry with a different payload is refused (the ACRFence action-replay attack). The undo is verified by reading back each record and the whole frame. Irreversible writes wait in a cancelable holdback queue. A REST `replace` update or delete is `VERIFIED` only on a route whose `precondition` (`If-Match`) has enforcement evidence: a recorded probe, or a probe the adapter runs once per route. Without it the write is at best `COMPLETED_UNVERIFIED`, since another caller's edit after the plan read could be erased unseen. A REST undo sends the version it checked, and an undo without an enforced precondition ends `COMPLETED_UNVERIFIED`, never `ROLLED_BACK`. A SQL write whose rows change outside the current schema is refused, PostgreSQL deferred constraint triggers included. A SQL write is `VERIFIED` only when the catalog shows nothing that could write outside the frame; no function body is read to decide that. On PostgreSQL: no user-defined object (oid 16384 or more, any namespace) reachable through `pg_depend` from the frame relations, no user column type, no user function or SQL-running built-in in the planned statement as `EXPLAIN (VERBOSE)` resolves it, no planned DDL, and no event trigger, user cast or operator, foreign table, `dblink` or `postgres_fdw` in the database. On MySQL: database-level `SELECT` and `TRIGGER` grants, and no routines. Any trigger on a frame relation (MySQL: in the database) caps the write. The inventory is read before and after the write in its transaction, and a change between the two to the triggers, rules, casts, event triggers or column types that decide what the write runs caps it. An open item caps the write at `COMPLETED_UNVERIFIED` with a `not_covered` code; it doesn't refuse it. Replays and adoptions keep these caps. The lab counts below predate these rules and were not rerun: the Vikunja lab spec declares a `replace` update with no precondition, so those updates and their undos now end `COMPLETED_UNVERIFIED`, and the Dolibarr SQL counts assume an empty scope inventory that was not measured | Experimental, this PR | Lab: Vikunja 2.7.1, Dolibarr 21.0.4 on MariaDB, Mailpit; 100 writes each; 0 missed effects, 0 false diffs, 200/200 verified undos (REST, SQL), 50/50 cancelled emails never sent, 50/50 released exactly once, 0/60 regenerated retries through (control 60/60 doubled), 0/10 after a crash after send; seeded faults caught 20/20 | `openadapt plan`, `openadapt_flow/txplan/`, [TRANSACTIONS.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/TRANSACTIONS.md) |

| One scoreboard comparing the agent alone with OpenAdapt across tasks (correctness by read-back, cost, time, items per hour) | Released ([#1303](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1303)) | Synthetic and local OpenEMR and openIMIS test copies | `benchmark/scoreboard/` |
| Pull a skill from the registry (`pull app/task@version`) and run it only after qualifying it on your own instance: `pull` marks it and expires any certification it carries, `skill bind` records your addresses and the names of the variables that hold credentials (never their values), `skill qualify` runs its bundled record check there, and `run`, `replay`, `emit-skill`, `emit-mcp` and `openadapt-agent` refuse it until then, and on any other instance. `openadapt-agent` refuses it before Flow starts, with reason `not_ready_to_run` and failed check `skill_not_qualified`, and refuses a pulled skill when no app address is set. The index and its archives carry a keyless Sigstore attestation from the registry release workflow, checked offline against a pinned identity, and expire and can't be rolled back; a release refuses a planned entry, and a re-stamp release (`registry-restamp-*`) renews the expiry and refuses any other change; a shipped record check runs no code and reads only your binding | Released; the `openadapt-agent` check, and a qualified skill passing the check, on main ([#2261](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/2261)) | Unit tests; agent path through the real `openadapt-flow run` process | `openadapt-flow skill`, [SKILLS_REGISTRY.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/design/SKILLS_REGISTRY.md) |

| Named sections for every compiled program ("Who: title, first name, last name", "Contact", "Create New Patient"), found without a model from the save, the recorded form structure, the fields and any narration; a person can rename, merge or split them on the review screen | Released | Unit tests; the certified OpenEMR referral bundle and a real recording of it on a local test copy with made-up patients | `openadapt-flow sections`; [SECTIONS.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/SECTIONS.md) |
| Encrypt PHI at rest by default: every bundle file that can hold patient data under one sealed index (unknown files refused), web recordings from the first frame, desktop recordings once converted, and every run directory; compile, induce, scaffold-verifier, qualify, admit, run, resume, undo, visualize, explain, emit-skill, for-each, sections, check mark, compose, process, variants, route, teach and push read them in memory through one artifact reader and refuse without the key; teach keeps its skill library and taught bundle sealed, and push keeps its sanitized review copy and approved archive encrypted until the upload | On main | Synthetic (no-plaintext audit-hook test over record, compile and a VERIFIED run; per-frame cost measured) | `openadapt-flow seal`, `record`; [phi_at_rest.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/phi_at_rest.md) |
| Encryption at rest by default, through a key hierarchy (sealed-set v3): each recording, bundle and run has its own data key, wrapped with HPKE (P-256, HKDF-SHA256, AES-256-GCM) to a per-set bucket key, whose record is wrapped to the device runtime key (only while the set is written), the device viewer key, organization keys (P-256 or RSA-OAEP-3072, required in organization mode with a key archive, from a machine policy) and a solo recovery key; files are Tink AES-256-GCM-HKDF 1 MiB streams. The device key is a software P-256 key in the OS keychain (or a 0600 file with a warning): the Secure Enclave, TPM, Touch ID and Windows Hello providers are interfaces with test doubles, not built. `at-rest shred` authenticates the set's header, then destroys its tracked bucket-key copies, in the archive the set was written to (an archive counts only with its marker file), and the run's checkpoints, which are keyed from the run's own data key. Receipts stay plaintext, over the plaintext report digest. `OPENADAPT_ENCRYPT_AT_REST=0` or `--no-encrypt` turns it off with a one-line warning and a ledger line | On main ([#2423](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/2423)) | Synthetic (hierarchy, fail-closed, org-mode, recovery, shred, unmounted and moved archive, whole-set substitution, backlog race and forged-header tests with test-double device keys and an injected keychain; payload checked against Tink); one headless MockMed quickstart with only ciphertext screenshots on disk | `openadapt-flow at-rest`; `openadapt_flow.key_hierarchy`; [phi_at_rest.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/phi_at_rest.md#key-hierarchy) |
| Model calls fail closed: a component with no `MAY_EGRESS` marker counts as sending frames off the box and needs the egress opt-in; a model "yes" from the drift oracle is a hint for the person reviewing the halt, never a pass; identity-VLM calls count as model calls, split by placement (off-box into `model_calls`, in process into `local_model_calls`), so off-box identity crops never report no external calls; every frame sent off the box is first written to a local append-only ledger (`egress-ledger.jsonl` beside the run directory, hashes and sizes only) and is not sent if that write fails; a signed record that counts off-box model calls must say external calls were observed, while in-process calls never require it; the regulated profile refuses a cleartext appliance or grounding endpoint that is not loopback; a pinned grounding model that can't be wired, or names no model, never falls back to a default model or to the appliance | Branch ([#2497](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/2497)) | Unit tests (`tests/test_model_failclosed.py`, `tests/test_drift_oracle.py`) | `runtime/model_egress.py`, `model_transport.py`, `model_call_evidence.py`, [ON_PREM_VLM.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/deployment/ON_PREM_VLM.md) |
| Receipts: one signed record per run, with any outcome (`receipt.json`, a DSSE envelope over an in-toto `record/run/v1` statement): one line per write with its check, strength and what it didn't check; digests, enums, counts and salted commitments only, never screenshots, typed values, URLs or page text; the outcome copied, never upgraded; signer roles from a pinned registry (this computer, customer key, OpenAdapt Cloud countersignature, public log, demo), unknown key, role or schema fails closed; a public card is the same envelope with only allow-listed values opened (`openadapt.public-disclosure/v1`) | Branch ([#2394](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/2394)) | Unit tests with synthetic runs (stopped runs, tampered report and payload, unknown signer, embedded image refused); 15 shared vectors for the Python, Cloud and web verifiers | `openadapt verify <file\|folder\|link>`, `openadapt receipt verify\|view\|publish\|unpublish`; [RECEIPTS.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/RECEIPTS.md); [vectors](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/types/tests/vectors/record-run-v1/README.md) |
| Older signed formats still verify, labelled "older format": offline and public Seals (`local-seal/v1`, `public-seal/v1`), Cloud-signed Execute receipts (`seal-signature/v1`), run summaries (`run-receipt/v2`), write and transaction receipts; Seals countersigned and timestamped | Released | Unit tests, real TSA tokens | `openadapt verify`; `openadapt-flow countersign`, `local-seal`; [OFFLINE_SEALS.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/OFFLINE_SEALS.md) |

## Every command, by capability

Each `openadapt-flow` command, grouped by the capability it serves. Each
command has one file under
[`packages/flow/docs/commands/`](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/commands/): to add a
command, add `<group>/<verb>.md` and run `python scripts/build_command_map.py`.
A test fails when a command has no file or this list is out of date.

<!-- BEGIN generated by scripts/build_command_map.py -->

**Record and build a program:**

- `browser-accessibility`: On Linux, make Chrome, Chromium, Edge and Brave start with their page readable to accessibility tools, so `record` can read what you click in your everyday browser. It writes launcher entries in your own `~/.local/share/applications` only; `--disable` removes them. On Windows and macOS, `record` does this by itself.
- `compile-agent`: With `--config DEPLOY_YAML`, the agent drives a desktop, RDP or Citrix app built by `build_backend`. With `admit TASK_DIR`, a person confirms and admits a waiting draft, such as one an agent taught over MCP (`openadapt-agent serve --teach`).
- `compile`
- `compose`
- `confirm-surfaces`: Show the windows and apps a cross-window recording used, with the steps on each, and confirm them. `compile` refuses a cross-window recording until a person has confirmed its surfaces, either at the end of `record` or with this command. `--yes` confirms without asking.
- `demo-record`
- `disambiguate`
- `for-each`
- `induce`
- `intake`
- `narration`
- `process`
- `pull`: Download a workflow from the registry, after checking the attested index and every file against it. The pulled copy does not run, here or through `openadapt-agent`, until `skill qualify` passes on your own instance.
- `record`
- `route`
- `sections`: Show, rename, merge or split the named sections a program map folds
- `skill`: Bind a pulled skill to your instance, qualify it there, and check whether it may run.
- `variants`
- `visualize`

**Check and admit:**

- `admit`
- `api`
- `approver-grant`
- `bind-record-checks`
- `certify`
- `check`
- `jit`
- `known-ids`
- `lint`
- `onboard`: Synthesize and planted-fault-qualify a verification pack for any system of record.
- `propose-qualification`
- `qualify`
- `scaffold-verifier`
- `teach-authorization`

**Run and answer:**

- `approve`
- `business-decisions`
- `console`
- `deferred`
- `exceptions`: Let any agent stop and ask a person: `serve` runs the `raise_exception` MCP tool, `watch` raises cards from a Chromium agent's page without the agent and blocks its saves while one is open, `list` shows waiting cards, and `answer` writes one closed answer signed with an approver key. A run goes on only after a verified `continue` or `done_by_person`. See `packages/flow/docs/EXCEPTION_QUEUE.md`.
- `explain`
- `item-approval`
- `replay`
- `resume`
- `run`
- `triage`

**Judge any executor's write:**

- `reconcile`: Check that the EHR, clearinghouse and payer agree on one prior authorization or claim, and report each break.
- `serve-reward`: Scores agent training episodes by reading the system of record.
- `verify-run`

**Repair and learn from halts:**

- `cleanup`: A clean screen after a halted item; `cleanup qualify` tries the halt cleanup on a test copy after every step and stores it when the start screen always comes back and no record changes.
- `fleet`
- `repair`
- `rollback`: Compensating rollback after a stop; `rollback qualify` stops the run before and after every save on a test copy and keeps the compensations that restore the whole database.
- `teach-branch`
- `teach`
- `undo`: The undo steps a person approves after a stop; `undo propose` finds and verifies them on a test copy, `undo accept` is a person's one-time approval of a proposal.

**Give agents the program:**

- `emit-mcp`: Write a standalone MCP `server.py` for one bundle. A pulled workflow is refused until `skill qualify` has passed, and the server refuses a run on any other app address.
- `emit-skill`: Write an Agent Skills folder for one bundle. A pulled workflow is refused until `skill qualify` has passed.
- `handoff`: Agent-to-agent handoffs: `send` attaches a run's receipt to what one agent hands another (inline, detached beside a file, or POSTed to a webhook); `verify` checks one on arrival against your pinned keys (who signed, what was checked, and that a valid signature proves who signed, not that the claim is true); `key` and `trust` exchange receipt keys between parties; `list` shows handoffs to other parties and what their systems confirmed.
- `serve-execute`: With `--config DEPLOY_YAML`, a bundle recorded on Windows, macOS, Linux, RDP or Citrix runs through `openadapt-flow run --config`, under its admission's qualification authority.
- `wrap-dispatch`: Run a wrapped task's admitted program only; a miss runs nothing. With `--fallback agent --fallback-max-cost-usd N`, a proved pre-effect drift goes to the agent behind a pre-commit gate (the terminal, or `--fallback-gate item-approval` for a signed approval from a phone or `item-approval approve`); `status`, `release` and `evict` manage the hold (docs/WRAP_FALLBACK.md).

**Proof:**

- `attach-seal`
- `countersign`
- `encrypt`
- `ledger`: Per-run accounting rows for any executor: outcome (VERIFIED, ESCALATED, CAUGHT_ERROR, FAILED, UNKNOWN), a person's minutes, model cost, fields checked; no record values
- `local-seal`: Offline Seals: customer-held keys, pinned verification, Rekor anchoring, run authorizations, operator profiles, public cards.
- `receipt`: Signed write receipts (COSE, SCITT shape): check one offline against pinned keys and print what it did not check; export the public keys; anchor in Rekor.
- `redact-report`: Strip session tokens from an existing run's report so it can be sealed again; the original stays local
- `seal`: Hidden alias of `encrypt` for one release.

**Run on premises:**

- `at-rest`: Encryption at rest: the device keys, policy and recipients by fingerprint, a solo recovery key, `restore` for a backup only the recovery code opens, and `shred`, which destroys an encrypted run's bucket key so nobody can open it.
- `no-outbound`
- `service`

**Share safely with OpenAdapt Cloud:**

- `approve-sanitized`
- `connect`
- `connector`: Run an outbound connector with local secrets, pinned admission keys, signed requests, token rotation, heartbeats and cancellation.
- `login`
- `materialize-approved`
- `push`
- `report-break`
- `report-run`
- `review-sanitized`
- `sanitize`
- `validate-hosted`

**Try it and measure it:**

- `bench`
- `benchmark`
- `demo`
- `silent-saves`: Scores any GUI agent on injected bad saves, from the source checkout.
- `tutorial`

**Guard an agent you already run:**

- `flight`: Record any agent you already run: meter and price its model calls through a loopback proxy, scrub its text and PNG/JPEG/GIF/BMP/TIFF/WEBP screenshots before they leave the machine, block other egress on macOS, log its actions, and hold each click that is not known to be safe for a person.
- `guard`: Attaches to the agent's own Chromium over CDP, holds each save until the right record is on screen, reads it back, writes a ledger row and a private diff, and hands a verified run to the teach dir.
- `hooks`: Writes `openadapt.systems.yaml` checks into Claude Code or Codex hooks: each write to a declared database, HTTP API or MCP tool is pre-checked, read back and given a signed receipt (advisory).
- `learn`: Learn the app's own per-request writes from a shadow run or from read-only requests (`learn probe`), and write them into the contracts.
- `plan`: Dry-runs a batch of writes to external systems (REST APIs, SQL databases, email) and prints what would change; applies it only under a single-use approval bound to the plan digest, with an idempotency key per write that a regenerated payload cannot change; undoes it with a read-back proof; holds email in a cancelable queue.
- `proxy`: Holds the database credentials, and with `--api` the API credentials, and runs the agent with scoped MCP tools: each SQL write is dry-run in a rolled-back transaction with its exact row-level diff, approved by policy or by a person against the plan digest, committed once only if its diff matches, and undone with a read-back proof; each API write is sent once under a task-derived key, read back, and checked against the system's own event or audit log.
- `readiness`: Shadow a candidate agent or compiled program on tasks a person did, stopped before every save, and write a one-page Readiness Scorecard (matched N of M, risks, field errors, time and cost).
- `shadow`: Shadow an agent: check each write it makes through an HTTP proxy, or check announced database actions for a desktop client, against the system of record without blocking it, and report.

<!-- END generated by scripts/build_command_map.py -->

## Measured results

- **OpenEMR referral, 62 timed runs each, warm.** OpenAdapt took a median of
  29.7 s and a computer-use agent (Claude) 36.5 s. Both saved 62 of 63
  referrals correctly. OpenAdapt made no model calls; the agent cost about
  $0.08 per referral. Raw data and
  figures: [benchmark/openemr_referral_timing](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/benchmark/openemr_referral_timing/).
- **Guard an agent you already run, MockMed.** A scripted Playwright agent
  in its own browser, 90 runs at a high shared load (median load average 29).
  Of the 8 `effect_e2e` faults that leave a wrong record, the agent alone
  reported 6 as saved; with the guard, the read-back caught 7 and 1 (a stray
  write to a table the REST read doesn't cover) got through; the compiled
  program caught all 8. The guard blocked the saves it can see: a save on the
  wrong patient and a second submit. Same-load pairs: the guarded agent took
  6.3 s (6 actions, each a model call for a real agent), the compiled tool
  4.4 s with no model calls:
  [GUARD_AN_AGENT.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/GUARD_AN_AGENT.md#measured-on-mockmed).
- **Fault test.** We injected 8 kinds of bad save, 9 runs each, alongside
  clean runs: 72 runs left a wrong record behind. A check that trusts the screen's "Saved" banner reported 54 of those
  as success; reading the record back over the app's REST API missed 9; the
  complete database read path caught all 72. The test app's database is
  SQLite with two record tables, so "every table" there is two tables.
  Separately, 9 of the 18 correct saves stopped in every arm: the server
  committed the save but its answer timed out, so the write step halted before
  any read-back ran. The count is of end-to-end run outcomes. The fault set and method are in
  [EFFECT_E2E.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/benchmark/effect_e2e/EFFECT_E2E.md).
- **OpenEMR referral: agent, screen program and API step.** Median wall time
  per referral, from a fresh browser through sign-in, the entry and the read-back:
  agent alone 36.5 s (62 of 63 correct, the 14 to 15 Oct study); compiled program
  on the screen 22.5 s (18 of 18); the same program with the API step 3.3 s
  (18 of 18). The program rows ran on 19 Oct, interleaved on one copy, with
  the approval gate off; the benchmark harness admitted the API step:
  [SCOREBOARD.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/benchmark/scoreboard/SCOREBOARD.md#openemr-agent-screen-program-and-api-step).
- **An agent's claims versus the read-back, on OpenEMR.** With faults injected
  in the fixture's database (partial, wrong value, duplicate, not persisted,
  another chart deleted, another chart edited; 5 items each), Claude Sonnet 5.5
  computer use claimed success on all 30 bad saves. `verify-run` caught 25 and
  confirmed 5 of 5 clean saves with no false alarms:
  [SCOREBOARD.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/benchmark/scoreboard/SCOREBOARD.md#the-agents-claims-versus-the-read-back).
- **An agent's claims versus the read-back.** Claude Sonnet 5.5 computer use,
  working alone on a test app whose server broke the save in 6 ways (5 items
  each), reported all 30 bad saves as done. `verify-run` flagged all 30 and
  confirmed all 10 clean saves, with no false alarms. The app shows "saved"
  before the server answers, so this measures what the screen can't show, not
  the agent's care:
  [SCOREBOARD.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/benchmark/scoreboard/SCOREBOARD.md#the-agents-claims-versus-the-read-back).
- **openIMIS claims.** On a test copy of openIMIS, the open-source insurance
  and claims system that runs Nepal's national health insurance scheme, the
  compiled program entered 149 synthetic claims with no model calls: 148 read
  back correct and none were saved wrong. Each saved claim was read back by
  SQL through a read-only database role on the test copy; the 149th stopped
  before saving:
  [SCOREBOARD.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/benchmark/scoreboard/SCOREBOARD.md#openimis).

The systems each result ran on are listed in
[LIMITS.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/LIMITS.md#validated-on).

<!-- Surfaces: packages/flow/docs/SURFACES.md -->

# Execution surfaces

OpenAdapt drives six execution surfaces through one governed runtime:
`web`, `windows`, `macos`, `linux`, `rdp`, and `citrix`. The browser is one
surface among six, not a privileged default.

[BACKEND_PARITY.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/BACKEND_PARITY.md) lists every command and Python entry
point against the six surfaces: tested, works, or refused with its reason.

## Surface selection is explicit in production

- Under `--profile standard` or `--profile regulated`, `record` and `run`
  REFUSE to proceed without an explicit target: pass `--backend` (one of
  `web`, `windows`, `macos`, `linux`, `rdp`, `citrix`) or set `backend.kind`
  in the deployment `--config`. There is no implicit browser default in
  production.
- Under `--profile demo` (or with no profile, the permissive pre-profile
  posture), an omitted `--backend` records capture on this OS (`macos`,
  `windows`, or `linux`) and prints a visible notice. Pass `--url` without
  `--backend` to record the browser. An explicit `--backend` still wins.
  With `--profile demo`, the CLI also remembers your last explicitly
  selected target in a per-user state file
  (`~/.openadapt/flow_cli.json`, override with `OPENADAPT_FLOW_CLI_STATE`)
  and offers it as the default next time when that target is this OS, again
  with a visible notice. This convenience is CLI state only; it is never
  written into a workflow bundle.

## Workflows are bound to their surface

The recorder stamps the surface into the recording (`meta.json` `surface`),
and `compile` seals it into the bundle (`workflow.json` `surface` plus the
implied `execution_mode`). A workflow recorded and qualified on one surface
refuses to `replay`/`run` on another:

```text
run REFUSED: this workflow is bound to surface 'windows', but the resolved
backend targets 'web'. ...
```

Pass `--allow-surface-override` to proceed anyway; the override is recorded in
the run report (`surface_override: true`, alongside `recorded_surface` and
`execution_target_kind`) as compatibility evidence, so a cross-surface run is
never silent. A surface-bound bundle also supplies its own default target: an
unqualified `replay bundle` selects the bound surface rather than the browser.
Bundles compiled before surface binding carry no `surface` and behave exactly
as before.

A composition does not merge surfaces. `openadapt-flow compose` copies each
child bundle into a parent artifact; `run` executes those children one at a
time against the surface sealed into that child. There is no backend switch
inside a recording, and no parent-level `--backend` that retargets every
child.

## Execution boundary and evidence, per surface

Every substrate runs on the same small `Backend` protocol and the same governed
runtime. Each surface keeps its own deployment and evidence boundary.

| Surface | Execution boundary | Required workflow evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Browser (web) | Local, customer-controlled, or managed browser runner | Exact browser, application, environment, identity, effect, and policy contracts |
| Native desktop (Windows, macOS, Linux) | Local or customer-controlled | Exact host and application identity, native accessibility evidence, and an independent effect check |
| Remote display (RDP) | Local or customer-controlled | Exact client window or network session, remote-display identity, and an independent effect check |
| Citrix / VDI | Local or customer-controlled | Exact Workspace, server, application, display, identity, and effect contracts, with counted ICA/HDX trials |

Per-substrate engineering evidence is reported per the
[capability and qualification matrix](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/PRODUCT_STATUS.md):

| Substrate | Selector | Evidence basis | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Web / browser | `--backend web` | Required CI and third-party apps | The lifecycle on in-tree apps on every CI build; local runs on OpenEMR, Odoo, Frappe Lending and openIMIS test copies |
| Native macOS (AX) | `--backend macos` | Counted effects and a third-party app | 3/3 fixed TextEdit trials with exact file-byte effects, driving the backend directly; refused a two-window ambiguity without changing either file. On calibre (Qt, SQLite): record, compile and a governed run `VERIFIED` against its database; a same-title book by another author and two identical books stopped with nothing written |
| Native Windows (UIA) | `--backend windows` | Counted task acceptance | 3/3 fixed trials of an in-tree WinForms app in a Windows 11 VM, with independently confirmed SQLite effects; 3/3 refusal for both stale and ambiguous targets |
| Native Linux (AT-SPI) | `--backend linux` | CI on real AT-SPI and counted task acceptance | The `flow-linux-atspi` job drives a real GTK3 workflow through an isolated X11 / session-D-Bus environment (three verified effects, three ambiguous-target and three stale-target refusals), and records, compiles, runs governed and repairs a write workflow on a GTK3 app with SQLite |
| RDP (remote display) | `--backend rdp` | Counted task acceptance | Aardwolf RDP into a Windows 11 VM passed 3/3 fixed remote-input trials with independent guest-tools file verification; a separate real-FreeRDP batch covers record → compile → governed replay and refusal; through the stock Remote Desktop client on a real AVC444 session, 105 scripted runs saved 55 records confirmed in the database, with 0 wrong-record saves and 40 false stops |
| Citrix / VDI (pixel ladder) | `--backend citrix` | Required CI and counted no-DOM stand-in | Dedicated exact-Workspace-window driver, readiness gate, durable resume, and 3 healthy + 3 drift-halt no-DOM trials; the retained artifact records `ica_hdx_accepted=false` until a counted ICA/HDX run is attached |

[BACKEND_PARITY.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/BACKEND_PARITY.md) breaks this down by capability.
Every row is bounded to its stated evidence. Accepted application workflows are
qualified against their own controls, session/display policy, identity evidence,
and effect oracle; code-qualified Citrix deployments additionally attach the
counted ICA/HDX record for their exact Workspace/server/application matrix.
Details:
[`backends/RDP.md`](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/backends/RDP.md),
[`desktop/LINUX_NATIVE.md`](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/desktop/LINUX_NATIVE.md),
[`desktop/CITRIX_PIXEL.md`](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/desktop/CITRIX_PIXEL.md).

## What `record` observes

`record` opens the operator's real interface and watches what you do: real
clicks, typing, key presses, and scrolls, writing the same recording format
`compile` consumes. Perform the workflow, then press Ctrl-C (or close the
window) to finish. The `--backend` selector picks the substrate, and the same
selector is available on `replay` and `run`.

`--backend web` is browser-first (the app is a `--url`). For `windows`,
`macos`, `linux`, `rdp`, and `citrix`, the Capture component records local
screen, mouse, keyboard, timing, and available action-time structure.
`--macos-app` / `--macos-window-title` scope the macOS Capture window.
`--window` / `--window-title` scope a Windows-hosted local capture, and
`--rdp-window` / `--rdp-window-title` bind a local RDP or Citrix client window
to both capture and replay. `--task` records the operator's intent alongside
the demonstration. A compiled bundle is bound to the exact surface it was
recorded on.

`record` captures a person doing the task. An AI agent can show the task
instead, in a browser, a macOS, Linux, or native Windows app, or over RDP or
Citrix, through openadapt-agent's recording tools; see
[Recording on Windows, RDP and Citrix](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/RECORDING_ON_WINDOWS_RDP_CITRIX.md).

Install the Capture component together with the runtime for the surface that
will replay the workflow. Recorded parameter values become the defaults, and
`--param` overrides them at replay; see [`PARAMETERS.md`](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/PARAMETERS.md).

## First workflow, per surface

Each surface has an equivalent record -> compile -> replay path:

| Workflow surface | Exact install |
|---|---|
| Browser | `pip install 'openadapt-flow[browser]'` |
| Native Windows | `pip install 'openadapt-flow[capture,windows]'` |
| Native macOS | `pip install 'openadapt-flow[capture,macos]'` |
| Native Linux | `pip install 'openadapt-flow[capture,linux]'` plus the AT-SPI system packages in [`desktop/LINUX_NATIVE.md`](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/desktop/LINUX_NATIVE.md) |
| Network RDP | Recorder: `pip install 'openadapt-flow[capture]'` inside the demonstrated session; runner: `pip install 'openadapt-flow[rdp]'` |
| Local RDP/Citrix client window | macOS host: `pip install 'openadapt-flow[capture,macos]'`; Windows host: `pip install 'openadapt-flow[capture,windows]'` |

```bash
# Browser (Playwright / Chromium)
openadapt-flow record --backend web --url https://your.app --out rec
openadapt-flow compile rec --out bundle --name my-task
openadapt-flow replay bundle --url https://your.app

# Attach the same recorder to one existing signed-in local Chromium tab.
openadapt-flow record --backend web --url https://your.app \
  --browser-cdp-endpoint http://127.0.0.1:9222 --out rec

# Windows: Capture records the local window; the in-guest WAA agent replays it.
openadapt-flow record --backend windows --window "Target App" --out rec
openadapt-flow compile rec --out bundle --name my-task
openadapt-flow replay bundle --agent-url http://localhost:5001

# macOS: the app and title scope the local Capture window.
openadapt-flow record --backend macos --macos-app TextEdit \
  --macos-window-title notes.txt --out rec
openadapt-flow compile rec --out bundle --name my-task
openadapt-flow replay bundle --macos-app TextEdit \
  --macos-window-title notes.txt

# Linux: Capture records the local desktop; AT-SPI selects the replay target.
openadapt-flow record --backend linux --out rec
openadapt-flow compile rec --out bundle --name my-task
openadapt-flow replay bundle --linux-app gedit \
  --linux-window-title "Untitled Document 1"

# Network RDP: run record inside the demonstrated remote session.
openadapt-flow record --backend rdp --out rec
openadapt-flow compile rec --out bundle --name my-task
openadapt-flow replay bundle --rdp-host 10.0.0.5

# Citrix / VDI (one exact local Citrix Workspace window)
openadapt-flow record --backend citrix --window "Citrix Viewer" \
  --rdp-window "Citrix Viewer" --rdp-window-title "Ward A" \
  --rdp-readiness-text "Appointments" --out rec
openadapt-flow compile rec --out bundle --name my-task
openadapt-flow replay bundle --rdp-window "Citrix Viewer" \
  --rdp-window-title "Ward A" --rdp-readiness-text "Appointments"
```

The bound surface is the replay default, so `--backend` may be omitted on
`replay`/`run` for a bound bundle. During record, `--macos-app` /
`--macos-window-title` scope the macOS Capture window, and the local
RDP/Citrix flags `--rdp-window` / `--rdp-window-title` scope Capture and enter
the bundle's existing replay-binding metadata. `--agent-url`, `--linux-app`,
`--linux-window-title`, and `--rdp-host` are replay targets. The local Capture
session cannot control them, so `record` refuses them instead of accepting an
unused flag. Pass them to `replay`/`run`. Generate a draft with
`python -m openadapt_flow.cli_config init bundle --out deploy.yaml --backend rdp`
(or `citrix`, `macos`, `linux`, `windows`, `web`); fill `unresolved`, then
`run ... --config deploy.yaml --profile standard|regulated` wires the same
selection for a real deployment.

The browser attach mode keeps the Playwright-native recording contract. It
binds one same-origin tab and reuses the same event schema, DOM evidence,
before/after frames, secret redaction, compiler, and governed replay path as a
browser that Flow launches. Attach mode preserves a browser profile that has
already completed sign-in, SSO, or 2FA. The endpoint is local-loopback only, so
it refuses remote CDP endpoints. Flow refuses ambiguous same-origin tabs and
does not navigate or close the attached browser. You can resize the tab or move
its window between monitors: Flow waits for a stable CSS-pixel frame and binds
the next event to the new viewport. It refuses an action only if that action
overlaps the coordinate-space transition. See
[`BROWSER_RECORDING.md`](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/BROWSER_RECORDING.md) for setup, exact tab selection,
secret handling, and the boundary with the Capture Chrome extension prototype.

## The two remote execution modes

Remote systems (a Windows guest, a virtual desktop, a published app) can be
driven in exactly two modes, and the difference is a policy and capability
decision, not an implementation detail:

- **In-session** (`execution_mode: in_session`): the driver runs INSIDE the
  session it automates and uses the platform's accessibility / structured
  layer (Windows UIA via the in-guest WAA agent, macOS AX, Linux AT-SPI, the
  browser DOM). Choose this when policy permits installing the agent in the
  remote session; it enables structural resolution and structured-text
  identity.
- **External** (`execution_mode: external`): the driver runs OUTSIDE the
  remote session and drives the LOCAL client window (RDP client, Citrix
  Workspace) via pixels, keyboard, and mouse. Zero install inside the remote
  session; resolution and identity use the pixel/OCR ladder, with the
  documented pixel-substrate limits (`docs/LIMITS.md`).

The mode is fixed by explicit capability negotiation at qualification time,
recorded in the bundle (`execution_mode`), and never silently switched at run
time: `rdp` and `citrix` recordings are `external`; `web`, `windows`,
`macos`, and `linux` recordings are `in_session`. Moving a workflow between
modes means re-recording or re-qualifying it on the other surface (or an
explicit, report-recorded `--allow-surface-override`).

## Lookup capabilities: structure or pixels

To find a step's target, Flow first looks it up in the page or
accessibility structure (the browser DOM, macOS AX, Windows UIA, Linux
AT-SPI) and falls back to pixels. Structure is much more reliable where it
exists: on a desktop drift benchmark it found 21 of 21 targets where pixels
alone found 6 of 21. It does not exist over an RDP or Citrix window viewed
from outside the session; Flow sees only pixels there. A workflow qualified
with structure lookups could pass qualification and then fail in
production on that surface, so Flow checks for this.

**Declare the surface.** Set `backend.deployment_surface` in
`deployment.yaml`:

| Value | Means | Structure lookups |
|---|---|---|
| `local` | Flow runs on the same machine as the application | Yes, where the backend reads structure |
| `remote_in_session` | Flow is installed inside the remote or virtual desktop session | Yes |
| `remote_display` | Flow is outside the session, looking at its client window | No, pixels only |
| `unknown` | Not known | No: read as `remote_display` |

If you leave it out, `rdp` and `citrix` are `remote_display` and every
other backend is `local`. An `rdp` or `citrix` backend declared `local` or
`remote_in_session` is refused, because those backends always view the
session from outside. To get structure inside a Citrix or RDP session,
install the Flow runtime in that session and use its own backend (for
example `windows`).

**What qualification records.** `openadapt-flow qualify` records which
lookups the signed cases actually used (`structure`, `pixels`, or both) and
the surface they ran for, in the bundle's qualification project
(`workflow.json`, `qualification.lookup`) and in
`qualification/lookup.json`. A certification binds that record, so it can't
be edited afterwards without losing the certification. In `verify.yaml`,
`app.surface` takes the same values as `deployment_surface` and defaults to
`local`.

**The pixels-only pass.** Every `qualify` also runs the cases with
structure lookups turned off and reports how many trials still behaved as
required:

- When `app.surface` is `remote_display` (or `unknown`), the campaign runs
  only with structure turned off. That pixels-only result is the
  qualification: any trial that doesn't behave as required fails it, and the
  bundle is recorded as qualified on pixels.
- Otherwise the signed cases run with structure, and a second, unsigned pass
  runs them again on pixels. Its pass rate is for information. A low rate
  means the workflow depends on structure and will need its own
  qualification before it can run on a remote display.

The pixels-only pass turns off the structure step of the lookup only. On a
browser test copy, the identity checks and the guarded clicks still read
the page as they normally do, so the pass doesn't reproduce every difference
a real remote display makes.

On a browser today, the pass mostly fails. Under the Standard profile Flow
delivers a browser click only through an action bound to the page element,
and a click that pixels found has no such binding. On the MockMed demo the
pixels-only pass ran 18 trials and passed 0, each stopping at the first
click with "production action lacks a closed runtime actuation path". So a
web workflow can't yet be qualified for a remote-display surface through
the browser: with `app.surface: remote_display` the campaign refuses at the
first trial. That needs a qualification campaign driven through the RDP or
Citrix backend, which `qualify` doesn't run yet (see the limits in
[Qualify a workflow](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/QUALIFY_A_WORKFLOW.md#limits)).

**At run time.** Before the first action, a run compares the surface it is
on with the qualified record. If the workflow was qualified with structure
and this surface offers pixels only, the run halts with
`HALTED_BEFORE_EFFECT`, writes nothing, and the report tells the operator to
requalify the workflow for this surface (`app.surface: remote_display`) or
run Flow inside the remote session. A workflow qualified on pixels runs on
any surface. Bundles qualified before this record existed carry none and
behave as before.

The remote-display evidence for this check is synthetic so far: the tests
simulate a pixel-only surface, and there is no counted run against a live
Citrix deployment yet.

<!-- Limits: packages/flow/docs/LIMITS.md -->

# Limits and guarantees

OpenAdapt compiles demonstrated GUI workflows into deterministic, locally
executable programs. Healthy runs make no model calls. When an interface
changes, OpenAdapt can re-resolve a target from retained evidence, ask an
explicitly enabled model for a proposal, or halt for an operator.

This page defines the boundary of those claims. It is written for people
deciding whether a workflow is suitable for evaluation or deployment. It is
not a compliance certification, a safety case for a specific workflow, an SLA,
or evidence that OpenAdapt is appropriate for unsupervised clinical use.

For the current evidence behind each capability claim, see
[`VERIFICATION.md`](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/VERIFICATION.md). For the package-wide evidence map, see
[`PRODUCT_STATUS.md`](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/PRODUCT_STATUS.md).

## Validated on

Every published result used synthetic patients, claims and records.

| System | What ran |
| --- | --- |
| OpenEMR 8.0.0.3, local test copies (open-source EHR; its 7.0 release is ONC-certified) | Referral entry by agent, screen program and API step; injected database faults; repair of a relabeled save button; duplicate check |
| openIMIS, local test copy (open-source insurance and claims system) | Claim entry over a worklist; a relabeled Save sent to repair with no wrong save |
| A Windows 11 VM over Aardwolf RDP | 3 of 3 effect-confirmed trials (transport and input), plus a FreeRDP batch |
| Windows Server 2022 over RDP with H.264/AVC444, stock Remote Desktop client | 105 runs on two apps: 55 database-confirmed saves, 0 wrong-record saves, 40 false stops ([benchmark/rdp_avc_real](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/../benchmark/rdp_avc_real/README.md)) |
| Citrix stand-in, no DOM | 3 healthy runs and 3 drift stops through the Citrix backend |
| WinForms, TextEdit, a GTK3 app | 3 of 3 effects on each native backend |
| MockMed, MockLoan and fixtures (OpenAdapt's own test apps) | Fault suites, approvals, repair and the agent comparisons |

Each workflow is qualified on the customer's own system before it touches a
real record. Windows installers are unsigned and macOS builds are ad-hoc
signed; the Python packages are published from the reviewed release workflow.

## Product boundary

| Capability | Evidence basis | What the claim means | What it does not mean |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Browser record, compile, and replay | **Required CI and counted attach trials** | The launched-browser path runs end to end in automated and clean-environment tests. The attached-browser path reuses the same recorder and passes 3 real Chromium record-and-compile trials with secret exclusion and external-browser survival checks. A live resize case also compiles actions from two viewport and device-scale baselines. | It is not evidence for every site, browser extension, authentication flow, or long-running production workload. Attach mode requires a loopback CDP endpoint and one same-origin Chromium tab. An action that overlaps a resize is refused because its pre-action coordinate evidence is not exact. The custom Capture extension remains a prototype and is not a direct replay path. |
| Healthy replay with zero model calls | **Required CI** | A run that resolves from retained evidence can execute without a language or vision model; the run report counts model calls. | Zero model calls does not mean zero network traffic. The target application, hosted control plane, remote backend, or effect verifier may still use the network. |
| Deterministic re-resolution | **Required CI** | Bounded visual or structural drift can be resolved through non-model evidence and recorded as a reviewable change. | It is not general adaptation to a redesigned workflow, changed business rules, or missing evidence. |
| AI-assisted repair | **Required CI contracts; measured on synthetic apps; deployment evidence required** | An explicitly enabled model can propose a target or interpret a changed screen. Existing runtime checks still apply. Once a deployment names a repair agent, every stop that wrote nothing goes to it by default, and a person approves each fix unless a signed policy pre-approves its class. On MockMed's 22 drift modes, 6 of 21 stops that reached repair resumed and verified, with 0 wrong saves in 66 trials ([benchmark/auto_repair](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/../benchmark/auto_repair/README.md)). | A model proposal is not authorization, proof of identity, or proof that a business transaction succeeded. A stop after a possible write is never repaired automatically. The measured rate is for one agent on one synthetic app; it is not a field repair rate. |
| Human teaching and resume | **Required CI contracts; field evidence required** | A halt can produce evidence for an operator correction, guarded promotion, and durable resume. | Field recovery time, broad authoring UX, enterprise identity integration, and non-repudiation are not established. |
| Windows UI Automation | **Counted task acceptance** | The native UIA backend completed 3/3 exact effects in an in-tree WinForms app in a Windows 11 VM, and 3/3 refusals for both stale and ambiguous targets. | Acceptance is bound to the tested workflow and Windows environment; each application retains its own identity, effect, and version qualification. A qualification case pins the foreground executable's file digest, the machine and its exact OS build, so an OS update or a new executable needs a new qualification. For an app that a script interpreter, browser or shared runtime hosts, that digest pins the host executable, so the app's own release is pinned by requalifying it. |
| Native macOS automation | **Counted task acceptance** | The AX/AppKit backend, driven directly, completed 3/3 exact TextEdit file effects and refused an ambiguous two-window target; structural record/locate/refuse behavior is covered separately. Known AX-only ` - Google Chrome` and ` - Google Chrome for Testing` window-title suffixes are accepted only for the corresponding exact CoreGraphics application owner; PID, unique-candidate, focused/main, and topmost-window checks remain mandatory. | Acceptance is bound to the tested host and application. Accessibility exposure and supported native actions vary by application. |
| Native Linux automation | **Unit tests plus CI recording** | Root CI records under Xvfb and reads a GTK3 button over AT-SPI. Replay and the stops on ambiguous and stale targets are unit-tested with a fake AT-SPI client. | The built-in path is X11. Wayland needs an operator-approved portal session, and each application retains its own qualification. |
| RDP automation | **Counted task acceptance** | An Aardwolf batch into a Windows 11 VM passed 3/3 (transport and input) with an independent guest-tools oracle; a separate real-FreeRDP batch covers record, compile, governed replay, and drift refusal. | The records do not cover arbitrary applications, WAN conditions, or Citrix ICA/HDX. A real AVC444 session (same virtual network, software encoding) stops on 12 of 20 healthy OpenEMR runs; the causes are ranked in benchmark/rdp_avc_real. |
| Citrix / VDI pixel-window automation | **Required CI plus counted no-DOM stand-in** | The dedicated exact-Workspace-window backend, readiness gate, governed run, and durable resume passed 3 healthy effect-confirmed no-DOM trials plus 3 drift safe-halts. | The retained record explicitly has `ica_hdx_accepted=false`; live ICA/HDX acceptance stays bound to the exact deployment instead of being inferred from a stand-in or RDP. |
| Managed browser execution | **Separate product target and workflow admissions** | The hosted lane admits attested browser bundles; production mode requires a configured real runner and refuses silent mock fallback. | It does not extend the supported claim to Windows, RDP, Citrix, PHI-bearing shared-cloud execution, an SLA, or a regulated certification. |
| On-premises / customer-managed deployment | **Release and clean-machine evidence; site acceptance required** | Deployment configuration, local run gates, egress checks, and audit primitives are supplied. | OpenAdapt does not configure the customer's firewall, KMS, storage, identity provider, backups, retention, incident response, or legal compliance program. |
| Compose separately recorded bundles | **Required CI** | `openadapt-flow compose` writes a parent sequencer from named compiled children plus a handoff contract. Unit tests cover authoring validation, fail-closed missing-handoff HALT, and a two-child fixture whose second child is a local mock backend. | It does not merge two recordings into one backend, retarget a bundle onto a surface it was not recorded on, or introduce a process contract. Live Citrix, Production admission, and cross-application field campaigns are not claimed here. |

These evidence entries do not assign a product lifecycle state or accept risk.
An actively admitted release can still produce an unsafe workflow if the
demonstration, inferred checks, policy, or deployment configuration is
inadequate.

## Composing separately recorded bundles

`compose` sequences already-compiled children through the governed `run`
path. A child starts only after every predecessor ends `VERIFIED`, or a halt
class named with `--allow-halt`. A handoff copies an effect-bound parameter
from a confirmed receipt. Missing evidence HALTs. Subflows and worklists
stay inside each child, on that child's surface.

## Wrapped requests and verifier receipt bindings

`WrappedTask.verify_reply` associates reserved request context
(`ai.openadapt/request-context`) with verifier receipts and validates byte-level
digest invariants against the RunStore record. This mechanism carries the
following boundaries and residual security considerations:

- **Caller authentication**: Local bindings do not authenticate a caller,
  issuer, or signing key. A direct local MCP caller of a compiled server can
  supply `ai.openadapt/request-context` for any request whose run ID it knows.
  The stored digest in the RunStore prevents substitution or tampering after the
  fact, but the binding certifies only request-record association and byte
