  retried, and kept nowhere: not in a model's page listing, a screenshot, a
  log, a receipt or the recording. No source, an answer after the deadline, a
  decline, a multi-line or malformed answer, a field that changed while the
  person answered, an API binding on the step, or a backend that can't bind
  the field stops the step before typing, with a closed `second_factor_*`
  code. The action is new, so an older runtime refuses the bundle instead of
  skipping an approval. Over the control plane the code is sealed in the
  person's browser to a one-step P-256 key, and a cached run's child process
  gets the run token only with the control-plane URL. The wrap recorder turns
  a field marked `autocomplete="one-time-code"` into such a step. A code-only
  form's submit counts as a sign-in only once, right after a
  username-and-password sign-in. A field split into one box per character
  is refused. See docs/SECOND_FACTOR.md.
- An interactive run (a terminal on stdin and stderr) asks for a sign-in's
  second factor at that terminal when no control plane or command is set. A
  code is read without echo, under the step's deadline, in the calling
  thread; echo comes back on when the read ends, including on a timeout, and
  input typed before the prompt is discarded. On Windows the console is read
  one key at a time with `msvcrt.getwch`, which never echoes, under the same
  deadline and discard rules. A run without a terminal never
  prompts and still stops before typing. `OPENADAPT_SECOND_FACTOR_PROMPT=off`
  turns the prompt off.
- Effect locations (`openadapt.effect-location/v1`,
  `openadapt_flow/effect_location/`): the place a careful person would look
  again to see an intended value, stored as pack data. Each record holds the
  demonstration path and start condition (`same_screen`, `fresh_navigation`,
  `new_session`, `other_channel`), a locator (label, row key or region), the
  expected value, a codec (including a `template` codec that reads one
  summary row as two values and a `split_date` codec), the expected count
  and an optional baseline. `evaluate_all` judges every planned value as
  `held`, `refuted` or `not_checked`. A location that can't be reached,
  found or read is `not_checked`, never a pass. The check level comes from
  the start condition; the receipt word comes from
  `check_level.outcome_word` when it is available. The engine holds no
  application vocabulary: month names, yes and no words, currency signs and
  tables come from the pack. See docs/EFFECT_LOCATION.md.

### Changes

- Network captures no longer write raw bodies by default. `record
  --capture-network` keeps only the `--param` and `--identifier` values of
  each request and response body, plus a per-capture keyed hash of every
  other value and of each HTML, text or binary body; undeclared URL query
  values are hashed too. `dump_har` and `save_har` do the same with the wire
  policy's id and version fields. `--capture-network-bodies raw` (and
  `raw_bodies=True`) keeps the redacted bodies, which API step and undo
  proposals need, and is refused unless the recording is encrypted or
  `OPENADAPT_FLOW_PLAINTEXT_AT_REST` explicitly allows plaintext. Binary
  bodies, files and non-text responses are sized and hashed from their
  bytes as sent; the recording's `app_url` query is minimized too; an
  explicit `application/octet-stream` body is never parsed as JSON (a
  missing content type still is); and `load_har` refuses a HAR marked
  minimized that carries a raw body.
### Fixes

- `verify-run` with `minimum_effect_strength: independent_session` now
  verifies on a separate-session read (check level 3), as the runtime
  already did. Before, the two disagreed and verify-run never verified on
  it. The default minimum is unchanged (`independent_system_of_record`).
- The `tx` engine no longer caps every verdict at `UNCERTAIN` without a
  SQLite row authority. A post-commit API read sent with cache-bypass
  headers, showing no cache in its response, and whose record version is
  exactly one past the before-image's is `CONFIRMED` with basis
  `system_api`. Anything else stays `UNCERTAIN`.
- `verify-run`: an effect list that is empty, or tiers that don't pair one to
  one with the effects, is `INDETERMINATE`, `unknown` and `unchecked`, not
  `CONFIRMED`, `present` and `independent_readback`. The receipt model already
  refuses an empty list, so no run changes outcome today.
- `verify-run`: the effect folds settle against the planned effects, so a
  planned effect with no verdict is `INDETERMINATE`, and an observed-effect
  code nobody listed is `unknown` rather than `present`.
- The frame's version check: a duplicate version row, a version history
  that lost a row, or a changed target with no new version no longer hides a
  version saved by another user. The frame is refuted instead of not checked.
- Receipts: a line check nobody listed keeps the run from `VERIFIED` and is
  counted as not checked, so the three line counts add up to the lines.
- The form transaction layer (`form_tx`, an unreleased prototype until this
  release) reads back every field it typed, selected or kept. Each one gets
  a `passed`, `failed` or `not_checked` verdict; a field it cannot read back
  (no read-back declared, the summary control missing or ambiguous, a failed
  lookup, a value entered only in a popup) is `not_checked` and never
  passed. A submit with any `not_checked` field ends `readback_incomplete`,
  never `verified_done`, and gets no receipt. Before, fields typed in a popup
  estimator had no verdict at all and such a run could end verified.
  Popup inputs are also re-read just before the popup's apply button, and a
  mismatch stops the run before apply. The side panel shows refuted and
  incomplete runs as needing action. Measured on four held-out synthetic
  quote portals: `benchmark/form_tx_heldout_run/RESULTS.md`.
- A wrapped sign-in no longer compiles a pixel check that freezes a withheld
  credential field. The recorder blacks out a withheld field in every frame
  that still shows it, so a `REGION_STABLE` crop that overlapped one held a
  black rectangle that never matched the unredacted screenshot at replay
  time, failing a step whose region overlapped a credential box during the
  run, for example the click into the password field. Such a check is now
  clipped to the part of its region clear of the box and re-cropped from the
  same frame. When no usable part is left, it is dropped and recorded in
  `param_hygiene.json`. This applies to mined checks and to the
  focused-field pass.
- A FHIR searchset Bundle's `OperationOutcome` entry (`search.mode:
  outcome`) is no longer read as a marker match. Packs can declare
  `search_match` on the entry parent (Medplum uses `path: search.mode`,
  `equals: match`). A non-informational outcome is an error, not a
  found id, so recovery cannot adopt a write that never landed and an
  outcome id does not count toward `duplicate_write`.
- File, document, document-hash and email checks no longer claim
  `system_of_record` (tier 1) for every file. Their strength now follows who
  produced the artifact, set by the new `effects.artifact_producer`:
  `acting_session` and the default, `unknown`, are at most `same_screen`;
  `separate_session` is at most `separate_session`; `system_of_record` keeps
  tier 1. A store that overlaps `effects.acting_roots`, the user's Downloads
  folder or a Playwright download folder is graded as the acting session's.
  Under a declared `separate_session` or `system_of_record` producer, a scan
  that lists a file in a Playwright download folder beneath the store, or a
  file whose real path leaves the store, is refused:
  the verdict is INDETERMINATE and names why. Each verdict records the
  producer, and whether it was declared or observed, in
  `read_evidence.provenance`. Breaking: a deployment that relied on the old
  tier 1 for these kinds must now declare `artifact_producer:
  system_of_record` (one line in its `effects:` or `verifier:` section,
  including a `record --verify` file); until it does, runs that need a
  separate-session or system-of-record check are not `VERIFIED`. Verifier
  identities of configs that leave both new fields unset are unchanged.
